clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: 33–67% renal excretion; no adjustment required in isolated renal dysfunction (max 2g/24h if severe dual hepatic/renal failure)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Biliary elimination; monitor closely in severe biliary stasis and concurrent hepatic-renal failure
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Incompatible with calcium-containing IV solutions; absolute contraindication in neonates ≤28 days
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with lactation; excreted in low concentrations)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis via binding to PBPs (mainly PBP 1 & 2); active against Gram-positive cocci (MSSA, Strep) and select Gram-negative rods (E. coli, Proteus, Klebsiella)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion ~80-100% unchanged; dosage reduction required if CrCl <50 mL/min (q8h -> q12h-24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Low hepatic clearance; minimal hepatotoxicity risk; periodic LFT monitoring in prolonged therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Severe beta-lactam hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis; caution with nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Excreted in human milk in low concentrations; compatible with pregnancy/lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis; enhanced stability against beta-lactamases; active against H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, S. pneumoniae, and enteric GNRs
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: 66–100% excreted unchanged renally; dosage adjustment required in CrCl <30 mL/min (q12h to q24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic metabolism; transient asymptomatic transaminase elevations reported
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to cephalosporins/penicillins; oral axetil not bioequivalent mg-for-mg with IV/IM
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta; excreted in breast milk in small amounts; generally compatible)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs (PBP-3); potent bactericidal activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Gram-negative bacilli
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: 80–90% excreted unchanged by glomerular filtration; dose adjustment required if CrCl <50 mL/min to prevent neurotoxicity
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic clearance; monitor liver function during prolonged high-dose therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Neurotoxicity risk (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures) in unadjusted renal impairment; beta-lactam allergy
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Passes into breast milk in low concentrations; compatible with pregnancy/lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Zwitterionic broad-spectrum bactericidal action; binds to PBP-3 and PBP-2; active against both Gram-positive (MSSA, Strep) and Gram-negative bacteria including P. aeruginosa and AmpC producers
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: 85% excreted unchanged renally; strict dose reduction required when CrCl ≤60 mL/min (dose/interval titrations)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic metabolism; monitor transaminases in severe underlying liver dysfunction
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, status epilepticus) if under-adjusted for renal clearance; beta-lactam allergy
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Excreted in low levels in breast milk; compatible with lactation and pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Prodrug hydrolyzed to active ceftaroline; high affinity binding to PBP-2a (mediates MRSA resistance) and PBP-2b (PRSP); broad Gram-positive and Gram-negative coverage (non-pseudomonal)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Excreted primarily via kidneys (~64% in urine); dosage reduction required when CrCl ≤50 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic metabolism; transaminase elevation monitor if co-prescribed with hepatotoxins
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Direct Coombs test seroconversion; Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea; beta-lactam hypersensitivity
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Excreted in animal milk; use in human pregnancy/lactation when clinically indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting peptidoglycan cross-linking and activating autolytic cell wall enzymes
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily renal elimination via tubular secretion (60–90% unchanged); reduce dose or extend interval if CrCl <50 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism is minor (<20%); periodically monitor LFTs during high-dose prolonged regimens
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Accidental IV administration of repository forms is fatal; severe beta-lactam hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis risk
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Excreted into breast milk in low concentrations; compatible with pregnancy and lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis via PBPs; provides prolonged low bactericidal serum concentrations from depot site
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal tubular secretion; slowly cleared over 1–4 weeks following intramuscular repository injection
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic biotransformation; standard liver panel monitoring in extended therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: For IM injection only; IV administration causes cardiac arrest and death; verify negative aspiration
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta in safe quantities; therapeutic drug of choice for maternal and fetal syphilis)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis via PBPs; intermediate duration of depot release (~24h)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal tubular clearance; adjust dose or extend interval in moderate-to-severe renal failure (CrCl <50 mL/min)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Procaine moiety hydrolyzed by plasma and tissue esterases; negligible hepatic toxicity
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: IM use only; danger of Hoigne syndrome (neurovascular toxicity/psychosis) if inadvertently injected intravenously
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy; safe for indicated maternal and neonatal infections)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs; bactericidal against susceptible Streptococci
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion (~20–40% unchanged in urine); dosage reduction recommended in severe renal failure (CrCl <10 mL/min)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism ~50%; hepatic impairment rarely alters clinical dosing; safe hepatic profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Severe immediate-type beta-lactam hypersensitivity; decreased gastrointestinal absorption if taken with food
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Safe throughout all trimesters; widely used for streptococcal pharyngitis in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits transpeptidation enzymes (PBPs) in cell wall synthesis; broad Gram-positive and select Gram-negative coverage
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal elimination (~60% unchanged); dose reduction or interval extension required if GFR <30 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic metabolism (~10%); transient asymptomatic transaminase elevations occasionally noted
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Beta-lactam hypersensitivity; non-allergic maculopapular rash highly prevalent during infectious mononucleosis (EBV)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Excreted in low levels in milk; first-line antibiotic choice in pregnancy and pediatrics)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits cell wall synthesis by binding to PBPs (PBP 1A, 1B, 2, 3); bactericidal against Listeria and enterococci
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal clearance 75–85% unchanged; dosage adjustment required when CrCl <50 mL/min (q6h -> q8h-12h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minor liver excretion; periodic LFT monitoring during prolonged high-dose IV therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High incidence of non-allergic maculopapular rash in EBV/mononucleosis; anaphylaxis alert in penicillin allergy
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Extensively used in pregnancy; first-line therapy for intrapartum Listeria and GBS prophylaxis)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds PBPs; steric hindrance of bulky acyl side-chain prevents inactivation by staphylococcal beta-lactamase
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Dual elimination: renal tubular excretion (30–45%) and biliary pathway; no adjustment needed except in combined failure
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Biliary clearance (~10%); cholestatic jaundice and hepatitis reported rarely; monitor liver function in prolonged therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Beta-lactam hypersensitivity; severe tissue irritation upon IV extravasation; phlebitis risk
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy and lactation; established track record in maternal mastitis)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis; acid-stable and resistant to staphylococcal penicillinase
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal tubular secretion (60%) and biliary elimination; dosage reduction rarely required unless severe combined impairment
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially metabolized by liver; safe profile but monitor hepatic enzymes during prolonged osteoarticular courses
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Esophageal ulceration risk (must take with full glass of water and stay upright); beta-lactam allergy
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy and breastfeeding; low breast milk excretion)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds PBPs inhibiting transpeptidation; isoxazolyl penicillin resistant to degradation by staphylococcal beta-lactamases
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion (50% unchanged) and biliary clearance; dose titration indicated in severe renal failure (CrCl <10 mL/min)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Idiosyncratic cholestatic jaundice and drug-induced liver injury linked to HLA-B*57:01; monitor LFTs closely
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: DILI/cholestatic hepatitis warning (may manifest up to several weeks post-treatment); hypersensitivity alert
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy; safe for treatment of staphylococcal skin infections in lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to PBPs (mainly PBP-3); extended spectrum against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Gram-negative bacilli
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal elimination 60–80% unchanged via glomerular filtration and tubular secretion; dose reduction if CrCl <50 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Biliary excretion accounts for ~20%; safe in isolated liver disease; monitor LFTs during intensive therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High sodium content (1.85 mEq/g); hypokalemia, bleeding disorders/platelet dysfunction at high doses; anaphylaxis
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta; excreted into breast milk in low concentrations; compatible)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Amoxicillin inhibits PBPs; clavulanic acid acts as a suicide inhibitor binding beta-lactamases, restoring spectrum
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Both components renally excreted; dosage reduction required when CrCl <30 mL/min; avoid 875mg tablet if CrCl <30
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Clavulanate-associated cholestatic jaundice and hepatitis; monitor LFTs if therapy exceeds 14 days
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with prior history of amoxicillin-clavulanate-associated hepatic impairment/jaundice
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with lactation; use in pregnancy when clinically indicated; caution with necrotizing enterocolitis in PPROM)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Ampicillin inhibits bacterial wall PBPs; sulbactam irreversibly binds beta-lactamases and has intrinsic activity vs Acinetobacter
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal tubular and glomerular excretion (75–85%); strict dose interval titration required if CrCl <50 mL/min (q6h -> q12h-24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic metabolism; monitor transaminases in patients on prolonged courses or concurrent hepatotoxic drugs
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Clostridioides difficile diarrhea; severe anaphylactic reactions; pain at IM injection site
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Safe and compatible across all trimesters; widely utilized in gynecologic and intra-abdominal protocols)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Piperacillin inhibits cell wall synthesis via PBPs; tazobactam inactivates class A and C beta-lactamases
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion (68% piperacillin, 80% tazobactam); strict dose adjustment required when CrCl ≤50 mL/min to prevent neurotoxicity
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic clearance; transient elevation in transaminases and bilirubin; monitor periodic hepatic panel
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Acute kidney injury risk heightened when co-administered with vancomycin; sodium load; severe anaphylaxis
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta; excreted in small quantities in milk; reserved for serious infections in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial PBPs; sulbactam inactivates bacterial beta-lactamases and exhibits synergy against GNRs
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primary elimination via renal route (>70% unchanged); dosage interval adjustment necessary if CrCl <50 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Favorable hepatic profile; lower risk of cholestatic jaundice compared to clavulanate combinations; check periodic LFTs
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Beta-lactam hypersensitivity; severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCAR); dose adjustment in renal failure
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy and lactation; used in clinical protocols for resistant upper/lower respiratory illness)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Reversibly binds to 50S ribosomal subunit (23S rRNA), inhibiting transpeptidation and bacterial protein synthesis
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily biliary and hepatic clearance; ~5–15% excreted unchanged in urine; no dose reduction required in mild-to-moderate renal failure
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Major hepatic metabolism (CYP3A4); cholestatic jaundice associated with estolate salt; monitor LFTs in prolonged courses
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor (causes serious interactions with statins, theophylline, carbamazepine); QT prolongation and torsades de pointes risk; gastrointestinal motilin stimulation causing cramps
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Estolate salt contraindicated in pregnancy due to risk of maternal hepatotoxicity; stearate/base safe)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to 50S ribosomal subunit, suppressing RNA-dependent protein synthesis; uniquely concentrated intracellularly in phagocytes with prolonged half-life
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily biliary elimination (~50% unchanged in bile); only 6–12% excreted unchanged in urine; dose adjustment only if GFR <10 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Extensively cleared via liver and bile; safe hepatic profile but idiosyncratic cholestatic jaundice and acute liver failure reported rarely
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Cardiac arrhythmia and QT prolongation alert; caution in pre-existing cardiac disease; myasthenia gravis exacerbation; low CYP3A4 inhibition
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Compatible with pregnancy and lactation; extensively validated in maternal chlamydial and respiratory infections)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to 50S ribosomal subunit; converted to active metabolite 14-hydroxyclarithromycin providing additive antibacterial synergy
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Dual hepatic/renal clearance (20–40% unchanged drug in urine); dose reduction by 50% required if CrCl <30 mL/min (reduce to 250mg q12h-24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Extensive hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4; monitor LFTs in co-morbid liver disease or persistent therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor (fatal colchicine interactions; statin rhabdomyolysis); QT prolongation; CLARICOR cardiovascular signal caution in CAD
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Teratogenic in animal models; avoid in pregnancy unless no alternative available; caution in lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to 50S bacterial ribosomal subunit, inhibiting translocation and peptide chain elongation; excellent acid stability and tissue bioavailability
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal clearance is minimal (~10% in urine); no dosage adjustment required in renal impairment
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Primarily hepatic metabolism and biliary excretion; monitor LFTs in patients with established severe hepatic impairment
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Mild-to-moderate CYP3A4 inhibition; avoid concurrent administration with ergot alkaloids; low risk of QT prolongation; high GI tolerability
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Animal studies show no teratogenicity; use only when benefit clearly outweighs risk; compatible in late trimesters)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds reversibly to the 50S ribosomal subunit, preventing bacterial translocation and protein chain synthesis; high tissue tropism particularly in placenta and reticuloendothelial system
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible renal clearance (<10% unchanged in urine); no dosage titration necessary in renal failure
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Excreted extensively via biliary route and liver; minimal hepatotoxicity; routine LFT surveillance during multi-month protocols
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Transient GI intolerance (nausea, vomiting); rare QT prolongation; does not cross the placental barrier efficiently to treat confirmed fetal infection (maternal-fetal transmission prevention only)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (First-line international standard of care for primary maternal toxoplasmosis acquired during gestation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds with ultra-high affinity to domains II and V of bacterial 23S rRNA in the 50S ribosome; overcomes erm(B) and mef(A) mediated macrolide resistance
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily eliminated via non-renal and biliary pathways; minimal urinary excretion; no dosage adjustment required across renal impairment stages
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Favorable hepatic safety profile without pyridine-moiety related hepatotoxicity seen in older ketolides; check baseline liver enzymes
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Engineered lactolide backbone lacks telithromycin cholinergic antagonist receptor affinity (minimal hepatotoxicity/visual disturbance/myasthenia risk); mild self-limiting GI effects
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B equivalent (Investigational / CDSCO Approved; avoid in pregnancy unless maternal benefit justifies potential fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) preventing DNA replication; narrow spectrum active against Gram-negative enteric bacilli (E. coli, Proteus, Klebsiella)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Rapidly absorbed and metabolized; ~80% excreted renally (partly active hydroxynalidixic acid, mostly glucuronides); contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) due to systemic toxicity
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic biotransformation to hydroxynalidixic acid (active) and inactive dicarboxylic metabolites; monitor hepatic enzymes in prolonged courses
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Severe neurotoxicity/convulsions in pre-existing epilepsy; intracranial hypertension/pseudotumor cerebri; acute hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency; tendonitis risk
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Contraindicated in 1st trimester; avoid near term due to kernicterus risk in newborns; cartilage toxicity in juvenile animal models)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, preventing DNA replication and transcription; potent concentration-dependent bactericidal action against Gram-negative rods (including P. aeruginosa) and enteric bacilli
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion 40–50% unchanged drug in urine via glomerular filtration and tubular secretion; dose reduction by 50% required if CrCl <50 mL/min (or CrCl 30–50 mL/min: 250–500 mg q12h; <30 mL/min: q18–24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism ~15%; substrate and moderate-to-strong inhibitor of CYP1A2; asymptomatic transaminase elevations common; rare acute cholestatic jaundice
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendinitis, tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, and CNS toxicities; myasthenia gravis exacerbation; aortic aneurysm/dissection; avoid with tizanidine/theophylline
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Avoid during pregnancy/lactation due to risk of juvenile arthropathy and cartilage erosion; reserved for anthrax or drug-resistant protocols)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; racemic mixture (L-ofloxacin is active enantiomer); broad spectrum against Gram-negative and atypical respiratory pathogens
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Extensively eliminated unchanged by the kidneys (>65–80% excreted in urine unchanged within 48h); strict dose titration required: CrCl 20–50 mL/min reduce dose to q24h; CrCl <20 mL/min 200 mg q48h
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minor hepatic biotransformation (<5% to desmethyl or N-oxide metabolites); periodic LFT surveillance during multi-week pelvic inflammatory protocols
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendon rupture, QT prolongation alert; CNS toxicities (seizures, psychosis); phototoxicity; avoid co-administration with Class IA or III antiarrhythmics
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Crosses placenta and passes into breast milk; cartilage damage in immature animals; contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (gyrA) and topoisomerase IV; localized concentration in urinary tract and gastrointestinal lumen; effective against Gram-negative enteric pathogens
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion ~30–40% unchanged drug via glomerular filtration and tubular secretion; dosage reduction to 400 mg once daily required if CrCl <30 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Biliary and hepatic elimination ~30%; moderate CYP1A2 inhibitor; safe hepatic profile; periodic liver monitoring in prolonged prophylactic courses
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendinitis, Achilles tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy; myasthenia gravis worsening; phototoxicity; crystallization in alkaline urine (maintain hydration)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Avoid in pregnancy and nursing mothers; risk of permanent joint and cartilage lesions in pediatric development)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; high systemic bioavailability and broad distribution into bone, prostate, and cerebrospinal fluid
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion is minor (9–15% unchanged drug); dose adjustment rarely needed in isolated renal failure; clearance delayed in severe uremia
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Extensively metabolized by the liver (~90%) via N-demethylation (to norfloxacin) and N-oxidation; dose reduction by 50% or interval extension to 24–48h required in severe hepatic insufficiency/jaundice
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Highest incidence of Achilles tendonitis and bilateral tendon rupture among 2nd-gen fluoroquinolones; severe phototoxicity; neurotoxicity risk
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Contraindicated across all trimesters of pregnancy and during breastfeeding; animal cartilage arthropathy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Difluorinated quinolone inhibiting DNA gyrase; extended post-antibiotic effect against Gram-negative urinary bacilli and ocular surface flora
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal clearance is primary (~70–80% excreted unchanged in urine within 24h); dosage reduction required if CrCl 10–40 mL/min (400 mg loading, then 200 mg q24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic biotransformation (<10%); monitor baseline and periodic LFTs in co-existing liver cirrhosis
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Extreme phototoxicity/photosensitivity reactions linked to difluoro-structure (must avoid UV light/sunlight); tendon rupture alert; QT prolongation
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Avoid throughout pregnancy and lactation; experimental models demonstrate articular cartilage degenerative lesions)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Pure S-(-)-enantiomer of ofloxacin; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; enhanced Gram-positive potency (S. pneumoniae) and atypical coverage
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Eliminated primarily unchanged renally (~87% excreted unchanged in urine); strict dose reduction required: CrCl 20–49 mL/min reduce dose to 500 mg initial then 250 mg q24h; CrCl <20 mL/min 500 mg initial then 250 mg q48h
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic biotransformation (<5%); low propensity for drug-induced liver injury; baseline liver panel advised in intensive care pneumonia
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, QT interval prolongation; dysglycemia (hypo/hyperglycemia alert in diabetics)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Crosses placenta and enters breast milk; cartilage degeneration in juvenile joints; avoid unless no therapeutic alternative in life-threatening scenarios)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; enriched Gram-positive (PRSP) and atypical activity (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella) with prolonged plasma half-life (~20h)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Dual elimination: renal excretion ~10% unchanged drug, glucuronide conjugates ~30%; dose adjustment indicated in severe renal failure (CrCl <50 mL/min: 400 mg loading, then 200 mg q48h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic glucuronidation (~30–40%); monitor transaminases in patients with underlying chronic liver cirrhosis
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Marked QT prolongation and risk of torsades de pointes; severe phototoxicity/photo-onycholysis; tendonitis and neurotoxicity warnings
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy and nursing mothers due to teratogenicity and neonatal cartilage injury)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: C8-methoxy quinolone inhibiting DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; bactericidal against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, atypicals, and anaerobes (Bacteroides fragilis)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Non-renal elimination predominant; ~20% excreted unchanged in urine, ~25% in feces; no dosage adjustment required across any stage of renal impairment (including hemodialysis)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Extensively metabolized via hepatic glucuronidation (14%) and sulfate sulfoconjugation (38%); no CYP450 involvement; avoid in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) due to metabolic saturation
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendinitis, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects; concentration-dependent QT prolongation (avoid in uncorrected hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia); myasthenia gravis alert
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Crosses placental barrier; cartilage erosion demonstrated in juvenile animals; use only if maternal benefit outweighs potential fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Dual affinity for bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; potent bactericidal against multi-drug resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae (MDRSP) and atypicals
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Dual pathway: renal excretion ~36% and fecal excretion ~61%; dose reduction by 50% required if CrCl ≤40 mL/min (reduce to 160 mg once daily)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism is minor; no significant CYP450 interactions; transient liver enzyme elevations noted; safe hepatic profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: High rate of maculopapular rash (especially in women <40 years or therapy >7 days); tendon rupture; QT prolongation; peripheral neuropathy
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Teratogenic potential in animal studies; avoid in pregnant or lactating patients; articular chondrotoxicity in juveniles)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Non-zwitterionic anionic molecule; inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV with equal affinity; active in acidic infection environments against MRSA and P. aeruginosa
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion 65% (unchanged drug and metabolites), fecal 28%; IV formulation contains SBECD cyclodextrin: contraindicated if eGFR <15 mL/min; oral requires no adjustment down to severe renal failure
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic glucuronidation primarily via UGT1A1, UGT1A3, UGT2B7; non-CYP pathway; favorable hepatic profile; periodic liver panel monitoring
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Tendinitis, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects; uniquely lower risk of QT prolongation and phototoxicity compared to older fluoroquinolones
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Animal studies show post-implantation loss and ossification delays at maternally toxic doses; use only if benefits justify fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Dual-targeting of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV; potent against quinolone-resistant Gram-positives (MRSA, VRSA, VISA) and respiratory atypical strains; active at acidic pH
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Eliminated primarily via biliary/fecal (~60%) and renal (~30%) pathways; no dosage titration required in mild-to-moderate renal failure; well tolerated in uremia
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism via glucuronidation; safe hepatic profile; monitor baseline and periodic LFTs in septicemia and bacteremic patients
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Novel entity; monitored for hypersensitivity reactions; lower risk of phototoxicity and QT prolongation; lack of CNS GABA receptor binding reduces seizure risk
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B equivalent (CDSCO Approved novel drug; lack of adequate reproductive data; avoid in pregnancy unless maternal benefit clearly outweighs fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase; potent bactericidal against Cutibacterium acnes, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and methicillin-resistant staphylococci
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible systemic absorption (<1% recovered in urine following topical application); no renal dosage adjustment required for dermatological use
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal systemic bioavailability; negligible hepatic biotransformation; exceptionally safe systemic safety profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with known fluoroquinolone hypersensitivity; local adverse reactions include contact dermatitis, erythema, burning, and pruritus
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Topical absorption is minimal, but avoid widespread or prolonged application during pregnancy and breastfeeding)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Dual synergistic action: Ofloxacin inhibits DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV; Ornidazole generates reactive nitro radicals causing microbial DNA helix breakage in anaerobes and protozoa
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Ofloxacin renally excreted (>70%); Ornidazole metabolised and excreted renally (60–70%) and fecally (20–25%); dose adjustment necessary if CrCl <50 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Ornidazole undergoes substantial hepatic biotransformation (CYP2A6/CYP450); monitor LFTs in underlying liver cirrhosis or prolonged therapeutic courses
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Dual CNS toxicity alert (seizures, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy); Disulfiram-like ethanol reaction; tendonitis alert; hypersensitivity warning
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Avoid in 1st trimester due to nitroimidazole mutagenic risk; contraindicated in nursing mothers due to high excretion into breast milk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Synergistic luminal antimicrobial: Norfloxacin targets bacterial DNA gyrase in enteric bacilli; Tinidazole causes free radical-mediated DNA strand breakage in protozoa and anaerobes
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Norfloxacin excreted renally (~30–40%); Tinidazole renally excreted (~20–25% unchanged); dose reduction or extended dosing interval required if CrCl <30 mL/min
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Tinidazole metabolized by CYP3A4; mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment alters drug clearance; routine liver panel surveillance advised
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Disulfiram-like ethanol reaction (strictly avoid alcohol during and 72h post-therapy); bitter metallic taste; Achilles tendonitis warning; CNS toxicity
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Contraindicated in 1st trimester of pregnancy and throughout lactation; nitroimidazole mutational concerns in early embryogenesis)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Comprehensive dual antimicrobial: Ciprofloxacin inhibits DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV vs enteric pathogens; Tinidazole generates nitro radicals lethal to E. histolytica and Giardia
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Both agents have significant renal clearance components; dosage interval reduction indicated when CrCl <50 mL/min (q12h to q24h)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Dual hepatic biotransformation; ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2; tinidazole metabolized via CYP3A4; monitor hepatic enzymes in prolonged therapy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Severe disulfiram-like ethanol reaction; severe tendonitis/tendon rupture warning; metallic taste; peripheral neuropathy and neurotoxicity alerts
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Contraindicated in 1st trimester and nursing mothers; animal juvenile arthropathy and nitroimidazole embryonic toxicity risks)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Reversibly binds to 30S ribosomal subunit, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA access to ribosomal A-site and inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis; bacteriostatic
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Excreted renally (~60% unchanged via glomerular filtration); accumulates in renal insufficiency; dose reduction or extended intervals required if CrCl <50 mL/min; contraindicated in severe renal impairment
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism and biliary excretion (~10–20%); dose-dependent hepatotoxicity (fatty liver change) reported at high parenteral or oral doses, especially in azotemic or pregnant patients
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Polyvalent cation chelation (Ca, Mg, Fe, Al impairs absorption); permanent tooth discoloration and enamel hypoplasia in children <8 years; pill-induced esophagitis (take with full glass of water)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Contraindicated in 2nd and 3rd trimesters; chelates calcium, deposits in fetal bones and deciduous teeth causing hypoplasia, growth inhibition, and maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds reversibly to the 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, blocking tRNA translocation and peptide chain elongation; broad-spectrum bacteriostatic against Gram-positives and Gram-negatives
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primary renal elimination via glomerular filtration; significant drug accumulation in renal failure; dose reduction required in renal dysfunction; avoid in severe azotemia
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially excreted into bile; monitor hepatic transaminases with prolonged systemic administration; elevated risk of hepatic necrosis with impaired renal clearance
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Severe local pain and sterile abscess with IM injection; chelation with dairy products and antacids; bone growth suppression in infants; photosensitivity and cutaneous phototoxicity
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Contraindicated during pregnancy; cross-placental transfer causes fetal skeletal development retardation and permanent yellow-gray-brown dentition staining)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by interfering with binding of aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosomal acceptor site on the 30S subunit; bacteriostatic topical antimicrobial
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible systemic absorption following topical skin or ophthalmic application; no renal dosage adjustment required for dermatological or ophthalmic preparations
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal systemic bioavailability from localized topical preparations; negligible hepatic clearance burden; safe systemic profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tetracycline derivatives; localized contact dermatitis, ocular stinging, erythema, and transient visual blurring; avoid systemic absorption over extensive open burns
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Systemic use contraindicated; topical ophthalmic/dermal formulation has minimal absorption, but use with caution and only if clearly needed during pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: High-affinity reversible binding to 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, preventing protein synthesis; high lipophilicity enables superior tissue penetration and intracellular pathogen eradication
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Eliminated non-renally via gastrointestinal tract and biliary excretion into feces as inactive chelates/conjugates (~70–80%); renal excretion ~20–30%; no dosage adjustment required in renal failure or hemodialysis
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially metabolized by liver; safe hepatic clearance profile; monitor baseline hepatic function in pre-existing liver disease; well tolerated across hepatic populations
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Severe pill-induced esophageal ulceration (must take with full glass of water and remain upright for ≥30 min); phototoxicity; benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri); antacid chelation
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Contraindicated in 2nd and 3rd trimesters due to tooth discoloration and bone growth inhibition; short-term use allowed in life-threatening Rickettsial infections like scrub typhus)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Reversibly binds to 30S ribosomal subunit inhibiting protein synthesis; highest lipophilicity among tetracyclines, crossing blood-brain and sebum-follicular barriers with marked anti-inflammatory properties
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily cleared non-renally via hepatic biotransformation and biliary/fecal excretion; renal excretion ~5–12%; no dosage adjustment needed in mild-to-moderate renal failure; use caution in end-stage renal failure
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Extensively metabolized in the liver; risk of drug-induced autoimmune hepatitis, lupus-like syndrome, and hyperpigmentation (skin, sclera, oral mucosa) on long-term therapy; periodic LFT monitoring recommended
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Vestibular side effects (dizziness, vertigo, ataxia—especially in women); blue-black hyperpigmentation of skin/nails/mucosa; DRESS syndrome; benign intracranial hypertension; chelation
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Strictly contraindicated during pregnancy; crosses placenta, suppresses fetal osteogenesis, permanently discolors tooth enamel, and presents teratogenic risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to 30S ribosomal subunit with 5-fold higher affinity than tetracyclines; N-alkylglycylamido side chain overcomes ribosomal protection and efflux-pump (TetA–E) mediated resistance; bacteriostatic
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily cleared non-renally (biliary and fecal excretion ~59%, unchanged glucuronate metabolites); renal excretion ~33%; no dosage adjustment required in renal impairment or end-stage hemodialysis
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Metabolized via glucuronidation; severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) requires 50% maintenance dose reduction (25 mg q12h); monitor LFTs and total bilirubin; high incidence of nausea/vomiting
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Increased risk of all-cause mortality compared to other comparators in severe sepsis/HAP; reserve strictly for multidrug-resistant pathogens (ESBL, CRE, MRSA); pancreatitis risk; lack of Pseudomonas coverage
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Contraindicated during pregnancy; embryofetal toxicity, decreased fetal body weight, delayed bone ossification in animal studies; tooth discoloration risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Dual protective therapeutic: Doxycycline inhibits 30S ribosomal protein synthesis; live Lactobacillus spores survive gastric acidity to germinate and replenish intestinal microbiome, preventing dysbiosis
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Doxycycline excreted predominantly via gastrointestinal chelation and biliary pathways; no renal adjustment required in renal impairment; Lactobacillus acts luminally without systemic absorption
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Doxycycline undergoes safe non-renal elimination with minimal hepatic risk; monitor baseline LFTs in chronic therapy; Lactobacillus has zero systemic hepatic impact
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Ingest with a full glass of water and remain upright for ≥30 min to prevent esophageal erosion; separate administration from polyvalent cations/antacids by ≥2h; photosensitivity warning
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Avoid during pregnancy due to doxycycline-induced enamel hypoplasia and fetal skeletal growth inhibition; probiotic component is clinically safe)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Irreversibly binds to 30S bacterial ribosomal subunit, inducing codon misreading, inhibiting translocation, and disrupting bacterial outer cell membrane integrity; bactericidal
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Rapid glomerular filtration of unchanged drug (>90%); CrCl >50: 15 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 30–50: 15 mg/kg q36h; CrCl 10–30: 15 mg/kg q48h; hemodialysis supplemental dose required; monitor CrCl, peak (20–30 mcg/mL) & trough (<5 mcg/mL)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic metabolism; no dosage adjustment required in hepatic impairment; safe hepatic profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Nephrotoxicity (ATN) and irreversible ototoxicity (vestibular and cochlear hair cell loss); neuromuscular blockade / respiratory paralysis (potentiated with NMBDs); avoid concomitant loop diuretics
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Crosses placenta; causes irreversible bilateral congenital neurosensory deafness; avoid unless treating life-threatening MDR infections where alternatives are unavailable)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Irreversibly binds to 30S rRNA of bacterial ribosomes, interfering with initiation complex formation and causing premature translation termination; concentration-dependent bactericidal
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Glomerular filtration of unchanged drug (>90%); extended interval (5–7 mg/kg q24h if CrCl ≥60) or conventional (1.5–2 mg/kg q8h); adjust dose/interval based on CrCl; target peak 5–10 mcg/mL, trough <1–2 mcg/mL
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: No hepatic metabolism; eliminated unchanged in urine; monitor baseline liver enzymes; low hepatic risk
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: High incidence of acute tubular necrosis and vestibular/cochlear damage; avoid rapid IV push; contraindication in myasthenia gravis; potentiates curare-like muscle relaxants
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Fetal damage demonstrated; placental transfer may lead to congenital eighth cranial nerve ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity; contraindicated in normal pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Irreversible binding to 30S and 50S ribosomal subunits, preventing initiation of peptide chains and destabilizing outer membrane; potent concentration-dependent bactericidal against P. aeruginosa
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Excreted unchanged (>90%) by glomerular filtration; reduce dose/extend interval in renal insufficiency (CrCl <60 mL/min); inhalation produces minimal systemic levels but requires caution in ESRD; target trough <1–2 mcg/mL
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic clearance; liver impairment requires no dose adjustments; monitor baseline hepatic panels
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and neuromuscular paralysis; bronchospasm risk with nebulized formulation (pre-treat with bronchodilator); do not mix with beta-lactams in same IV container
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Demonstrated risk of congenital deafness in human fetal exposure; contraindicated during pregnancy unless critical benefits outweigh severe fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds irreversibly to bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, causing miscoding and mRNA translation breakdown; engineered to resist bacterial aminoglycoside-inactivating enzymes with lower cochlear affinity
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renally cleared unchanged (>80%); CrCl >50: 4–6 mg/kg once daily or 2 mg/kg q8h; CrCl 20–50: reduce dose or space to q24–48h; requires TDM (target trough <2 mcg/mL, peak 6–10 mcg/mL)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Not metabolized by liver; safe clearance profile in hepatic impairment; monitor routine transaminases
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity risk (lower relative ototoxicity than gentamicin, but monitoring essential); neuromuscular blockage risk; contraindicated in myasthenia gravis and severe renal failure
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Placental crossing demonstrated; potential eighth cranial nerve damage and fetal toxicity; contraindicated in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds specifically to bacterial 30S ribosomal protein S12, preventing tRNA translocation and causing widespread mistranslation; active against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and select zoonoses
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Glomerular excretion unchanged (50–60% within 24h); CrCl >50: 15 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 10–50: 15 mg/kg q24–72h; CrCl <10: 15 mg/kg q72–96h; monitor BUN and creatinine closely
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible hepatic metabolism; well tolerated hepatically; safe in pre-existing liver disease
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Severe vestibular ototoxicity (vertigo, ataxia, tinnitus) higher than cochlear loss; nephrotoxicity; peripheral neuropathy, scotoma, and hypersensitivity reactions (eosinophilia, exfoliative dermatitis)
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Proven teratogen; severe congenital bilateral deafness and labyrinthine damage reported in offspring; contraindicated during pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds 30S ribosomal subunit, inducing irreversible conformational change that inhibits peptide chain synthesis and protein assembly; specialized activity against MDR-TB isolates
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Eliminated unchanged via glomerular filtration (>80%); dosage interval lengthened proportionally to serum creatinine (dose q[Cr x 9]h) or guided by CrCl; monitor creatinine and trough levels
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal to zero hepatic biotransformation; no dosage adjustment required for liver impairment
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: High cochlear toxicity causing permanent high-frequency hearing loss; acute tubular necrosis; curare-mimetic neuromuscular blockade; avoid co-administration with other ototoxic/nephrotoxic agents
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Crosses placenta, accumulates in fetal tissues, causes permanent fetal auditory nerve damage; contraindicated in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, overcoming aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes (AMEs) including acetyltransferases, phosphotransferases, and nucleotidyltransferases; bactericidal against CRE
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Excreted predominantly unchanged in urine; CrCl ≥60: 15 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 30 to <60: 10 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 15 to <30: 10 mg/kg q48h; contraindicated if CrCl <15 mL/min; monitor trough (<3 mcg/mL)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Does not undergo significant hepatic metabolism; CYP450 enzymes not affected; safe in liver impairment
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neuromuscular blockade, and fetal harm; higher mortality observed in bloodstream infections compared to colistin in trials; reserve strictly for MDR cUTI
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (May cause fetal harm including congenital eighth nerve deafness; pregnant patients should be advised of potential risk to fetus)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to 30S ribosomal RNA, causing mistranslation in Leishmania parasites and Entamoeba histolytica; disrupts parasitic protein synthesis and membrane structural integrity
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Minimal systemic absorption following oral ingestion (<100% eliminated unchanged in stool); IM formulation is excreted renally and requires careful adjustment (dose reduction based on CrCl)
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible systemic hepatic metabolism; oral form acts strictly luminally; safe in severe hepatic dysfunction
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Oral: Steatorrhea, malabsorption, abdominal cramps; IM: Ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and injection-site pain; avoid in intestinal ulcerations or bowel obstruction where absorption increases
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C / D (Oral formulation poorly absorbed and preferred in intestinal amoebiasis if essential; IM formulation crosses placenta and carries ototoxicity risk—contraindicated for Kala-azar in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Irreversibly binds bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit, suppressing gastrointestinal ammonia-producing flora (urease-producing bacteria) and sterilizing enteric pathogens; non-absorbed luminally
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Poor systemic absorption (~3%), but absorbed fraction is eliminated renally; in renal failure or extensive mucosal ulceration, drug accumulates, causing systemic toxicity; monitor BUN/Cr closely
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Lacks hepatic biotransformation; indicated therapeutically to reduce blood ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy; beneficial in portal-systemic encephalopathy
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Systemic ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity if absorbed across inflamed bowel mucosa or in patients with renal impairment; malabsorption syndrome with steatorrhea; neuromuscular blockade
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Risk of fetal harm and auditory impairment if systemically absorbed; contraindicated in pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds 30S bacterial ribosome, inhibiting protein synthesis in localized superficial staphylococcal and gram-negative cutaneous pathogens; broad-spectrum surface bactericidal
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible systemic absorption across intact skin; no renal adjustment needed; avoid extensive application over large open wounds or denuded burns to prevent systemic renal accumulation
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Zero systemic hepatic biotransformation; no hepatic risk
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High rate of localized delayed-type contact dermatitis and skin sensitization (allergic contact dermatitis in up to 10% of users); avoid application to deep puncture wounds or extensive denuded skin
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Topical absorption minimal through intact skin; use on minimal surface areas during pregnancy only if clearly indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Concentrated localized inhibition of 30S and 50S ribosomal subunits, providing rapid bactericidal clearance against ocular external pathogens including P. aeruginosa and S. aureus
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Systemic absorption through nasolacrimal drainage is minimal; no dosage adjustment required for renal impairment
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible systemic absorption; zero hepatic metabolizing burden
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Ocular hyperemia, lid itching, punctate epithelial keratopathy, corneal epithelial toxicity with prolonged use; transient blurred vision with ointment; remove contact lenses prior to application
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Negligible systemic absorption following topical ophthalmic administration; animal studies show no fetal harm; safe when clinically indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: High local concentration inhibits 30S bacterial ribosomal protein synthesis, providing broad surface bactericidal action against susceptible skin ulcers, burns, and superficial ocular pathogens
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible systemic absorption when applied to intact skin or conjunctiva; do not apply over large surface area burns (>20% BSA) due to potential systemic nephrotoxic/ototoxic absorption
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: No systemic hepatic clearance required; minimal systemic exposure
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Local irritation, ocular stinging, punctate keratitis, delayed corneal healing; potential cross-sensitization to other aminoglycosides; superinfection with fungi on prolonged use
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Low systemic absorption; safe for localized ocular/dermal use, but avoid applying over extensive denuded body surface areas)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Pure Neomycin B isomer that binds to 30S ribosomal subunit, causing translation errors and membrane degradation in cutaneous staphylococci and gram-negative wound pathogens
clinical_core.Primary Routes: Topical (Skin Cream / Ointment, Gauze Tulle Dressing)
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Poor percutaneous absorption across intact epidermal barrier; in extensive second/third-degree burns, absorption may occur—monitor renal markers if large wound areas are treated
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible systemic absorption; no hepatic involvement or toxicity
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Contact hypersensitivity, pruritus, localized erythema; prolonged open wound use may lead to systemic ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity if vast surface areas are treated; avoid in perforated eardrums
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Topical absorption minimal on intact skin; caution advised when treating extensive open cutaneous lesions during pregnancy)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Natural aminoglycoside related to gentamicin; irreversibly binds to bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit to eradicate localized cutaneous bacterial infections with potent antistaphylococcal activity
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Negligible systemic absorption through intact epidermal layers; no renal adjustments needed; avoid wide-surface application on denuded skin
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Zero systemic hepatic biotransformation; entirely safe profile
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Local skin irritation, burning, contact sensitization; discontinue if pruritus, maculopapular rash, or swelling develops; for dermatological use only
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Topical dermal exposure produces insignificant plasma concentrations; use with caution during pregnancy if clinically indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Sequential inhibition of bacterial folic acid synthesis: sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Both cleared renally (SMX ~80%, TMP ~60% unchanged/metabolites); CrCl 15–30 mL/min: reduce dose by 50%; avoid if CrCl <15 mL/min.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic N4-acetylation and glucuronidation; idiosyncratic hepatitis, cholestatic jaundice, and hepatic necrosis reported; monitor baseline LFTs.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, TEN); G6PD deficiency hemolysis; hyperkalemia; hematologic dyscrasias.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category D (Contraindicated in 1st trimester due to antifolate teratogenicity and at term due to neonatal kernicterus risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Synergistic parasitic folate synthesis blockade: sulfadoxine inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; pyrimethamine inhibits plasmodial dihydrofolate reductase.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Excreted predominantly by kidneys with extremely slow clearance (half-life 100–200h); contraindicated in severe renal impairment (CrCl <15 mL/min).
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially metabolized in the liver; risk of toxic hepatitis and cholestasis; monitor liver enzymes in repeated prophylactic courses.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: BLACK BOX: Fatal cutaneous eruptions (SJS/TEN); megaloblastic marrow suppression; avoid in sulfa allergy or severe blood dyscrasias.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Contraindicated at term due to kernicterus; safe for 2nd/3rd trimester intermittent preventive therapy in malaria endemic zones)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Colonic bacterial azoreductases cleave molecule into sulfapyridine (carrier/antirheumatic) and 5-aminosalicylic acid (topical anti-inflammatory in bowel wall).
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: 5-ASA and metabolites eliminated renally; dose adjustment recommended in moderate-to-severe renal impairment; maintain high fluid intake to prevent crystalluria.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic acetylation of sulfapyridine (rate dependent on acetylator phenotype); slow acetylators have higher toxicity; check baseline/periodic LFTs.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Sulfa or salicylate allergy; risk of agranulocytosis, oligospermia (reversible), hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency; orange-yellow urine discoloration.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta in small amounts; folate supplementation required to avoid neural tube defects; compatible with lactation in healthy infants)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Dual mechanism: slowly releases bactericidal silver ions binding bacterial DNA/cell walls, paired with sulfadiazine inhibiting bacterial folate synthesis.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Topical absorption across intact skin is minimal; if applied over >20% body surface area burns, systemic sulfa absorption occurs—monitor serum creatinine.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal systemic hepatic load under localized application; rare transaminase elevation with massive total body surface burn application.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Argyria (skin discoloration); transient leukopenia/neutropenia; contraindicated in term pregnancy, neonates ≤2 months, and sulfa allergy.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B / C (Contraindicated in late pregnancy near term and in premature/term neonates under 2 months due to kernicterus hazard)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Competitive antagonist of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA), preventing bacterial dihydropteroate synthase activity and stopping bacterial folic acid production.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Minimal nasolacrimal systemic absorption; no dosage adjustment necessary in patients with renal failure.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Negligible systemic hepatic biotransformation; zero hepatotoxicity from ocular topical drops.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Local stinging, burning, conjunctival redness; contraindicated in patients with documented hypersensitivity to sulfonamides; inactivated by purulent discharge.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Systemic absorption following eye instillation is negligible; safe for localized ocular infections when clinically indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Synthetic sulfonamide that diffuses through eschar and avascular tissue, disrupting bacterial folate synthesis independently of PABA concentrations.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Rapidly absorbed across burn eschar into systemic circulation; metabolites eliminated in urine; may cause metabolic acidosis in severe renal dysfunction.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Metabolized to p-carboxybenzenesulfonamide; does not induce hepatic injury.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Potent carbonic anhydrase inhibitor causing systemic metabolic acidosis and compensatory hyperventilation; severe localized application pain/burning.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Systemic absorption occurs from deep burns; safety not established in pregnancy; contraindicated near term due to kernicterus)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds to penicillin-binding proteins (primarily PBP-2 and PBP-3), inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis; resistant to hydrolysis by most bacterial beta-lactamases.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Approximately 70% excreted unchanged by kidneys; dose reduction required: CrCl 26–50: 1g q12h; CrCl 10–25: 500mg q12h; CrCl <10: 500mg q24h.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Metabolized (~28%) to inactive metabolite; transient reversible increases in ALT, AST, bilirubin, and alkaline phosphatase; monitor LFTs during intensive therapy.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to carbapenems/beta-lactams; severe seizure threshold reduction when combined with valproic acid (dramatically lowers valproate levels).
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Crosses placenta; excreted into breast milk in low concentrations; compatible with pregnancy when clearly indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Imipenem inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis via PBPs; cilastatin inhibits renal dehydropeptidase-I, blocking renal degradation and nephrotoxicity.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Eliminated predominantly by kidneys (~70% imipenem excreted unchanged with cilastatin); strict titration required: CrCl <50 mL/min to prevent neurotoxicity/seizures.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic biotransformation; mild transient transaminase and bilirubin rises; standard periodic liver profile monitoring.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Neurotoxicity and seizure hazard (higher than meropenem, especially in unadjusted renal failure or CNS lesions); valproic acid interaction.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C (Crosses placenta; animal embryo-fetal toxicity observed; use in pregnancy only when potential benefit outweighs fetal hazard)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds PBPs (PBP-2 and PBP-3) with high stability against extended-spectrum beta-lactamases; lacks activity against Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Renal excretion accounts for ~80% (38% unchanged, 37% metabolite); CrCl ≤50 mL/min requires dose reduction to 500 mg once daily (or 500 mg post-dialysis).
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially metabolized via hydrolysis of beta-lactam ring; rare transaminase elevations; safe hepatic safety profile.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Seizure risk in elderly or renally impaired patients; profound interaction with valproic acid resulting in breakthrough seizures; anaphylaxis alert.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (Animal studies reveal no teratogenic risk; passes into breast milk in low concentrations; compatible when indicated)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Inactivates PBPs (PBP-2, PBP-3, PBP-4), blocking peptidoglycan cell wall cross-linking; enhanced in vitro potency against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Predominantly eliminated unchanged in urine (~75%); dose reduction: CrCl 30–50 mL/min: 250 mg q8h; CrCl 10–29 mL/min: 250 mg q12h.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Hepatic metabolism negligible; minor beta-lactam ring opening (~15%); low hepatic adverse reaction profile.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: WARNING: Increased mortality observed in ventilator-associated pneumonia compared to imipenem (not approved for VAP); lowers valproate serum levels.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B (No evidence of teratogenicity in animal models; use in pregnancy when maternal therapeutic need clearly justifies fetal risk)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Binds selectively to high-molecular-weight PBPs (PBP-1A, 1B, 2), inhibiting bacterial peptidoglycan synthesis; stable against extended-spectrum beta-lactamases.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Primarily cleared renally (~60–75% metabolites and active drug in urine); dose reduction indicated in severe renal insufficiency (CrCl <30 mL/min: 150–200 mg q12h-24h).
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Partially metabolized by liver enzymes; asymptomatic transaminase elevations reported rarely; favorable hepatic profile.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Cross-allergy with penicillins and carbapenems; gastrointestinal adverse effects (diarrhea, abdominal pain); Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B equivalent (Insufficient clinical pregnancy trials; use during gestation only if potential maternal benefits outweigh risk to fetus)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Meropenem inhibits PBPs; vaborbactam acts as a synthetic cyclic boronic acid beta-lactamase inhibitor, protecting meropenem from serine carbapenemases (KPC).
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: Both components cleared unchanged renally via glomerular filtration (~75–80%); strict adjustment: CrCl 30–49: 2g/2g q8h; CrCl 15–29: 1g/1g q8h; <15: 0.5g/0.5g q12h.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Neither component undergoes meaningful hepatic biotransformation; monitor standard liver panel in ICU patients.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: Beta-lactam hypersensitivity; neurotoxicity and convulsions in unadjusted renal failure; marked decrease in valproic acid concentrations causing seizures.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category B equivalent (Insufficient human data; animal studies show no teratogenicity; reserve for life-threatening resistant gram-negative infections)

clinical_core.Mechanism of Action: Imipenem blocks PBPs; cilastatin inhibits renal DHP-I; relebactam protects imipenem from hydrolysis by Class A (KPC) and Class C (AmpC) beta-lactamases.
clinical_core.Renal Clearance & Adjustment: All 3 agents eliminated primarily via kidneys (~80%); CrCl 60–89: 1g/0.25g q6h; CrCl 30–59: 0.75g/0.1875g q6h; CrCl 15–29: 0.5g/0.125g q6h; ESRD: 0.5g/0.125g q6h post-HD.
clinical_core.Hepatic Risk & Monitoring: Minimal hepatic metabolism across all three active entities; transient transaminase rises; routine ICU hepatic surveillance.
clinical_core.Critical Alerts & Contraindications: High Alert: Seizures and tremors in pre-existing CNS disorders or uremia; severe valproic acid interaction; beta-lactam anaphylaxis.
clinical_core.Pregnancy & Teratogenicity: Category C equivalent (Imipenem crosses placenta with animal embryofetal loss; use in pregnancy only when alternative options are unavailable)

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Bacterial Meningitis (Empiric / S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2 g IV (Adult) / 100 mg/kg/day IV divided q12h (Pediatric)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High CSF penetration required; co-prescribe Vancomycin ± Ampicillin empirically per local resistance profiles

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated UTI / Acute Pyelonephritis (Enterobacteriaceae)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1 g to 2 g IV/IM once daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Step-down to oral targeted antibiotic once defervescent and sensitivity confirmed; monitor renal labs

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Surgical Site Prophylaxis & MSSA Bacteremia
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2 g to 3 g IV pre-op within 60 min of incision (weight-based: 3g if ≥120 kg); redose q4h intra-op
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Single dose to ≤24 hours perioperative (up to 4–6 weeks for bacteremia)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor surgical site, serum creatinine, and repeat doses during prolonged operative procedures

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia & Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 750 mg to 1.5 g IV/IM q8h (Inpatient) OR 500 mg PO q12h (Axetil out-patient)
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV, IM or PO every 8 to 12 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor respiratory status, sputum cultures, renal labs, and step-down timing to oral axetil

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia & Febrile Neutropenia
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2 g IV every 8 hours (infusion over 30 min or extended 3–4 hr infusion)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Perform therapeutic monitoring, adjust promptly for CrCl changes to avoid neurotoxicity, follow cultures

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Febrile Neutropenia (Empiric Monotherapy) & Severe Nosocomial Pneumonia
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2 g IV every 8 hours (extended 3-4h infusion preferred in critical care)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict therapeutic drug and mental status monitoring; calculate CrCl daily to avoid encephalopathy

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Bacterial Skin & Skin Structure Infections (ABSSSI - MRSA) & CABP
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 600 mg IV every 12 hours (administered via 1-hour IV infusion)
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 1200 mg / day (up to 1800 mg/day in unlabelled severe endocarditis protocols)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor baseline and serial CBC/differential for Coombs positivity, renal function, resolution of lesion

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Neurosyphilis, Severe Streptococcal Bacteremia & Infective Endocarditis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 18 to 24 million units IV daily (administered as 3–4 MU q4h or continuous IV infusion)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Continuous clinical and renal function monitoring; co-prescribe Ceftriaxone if indicated; watch for Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Early / Late Latent Syphilis & Secondary Prophylaxis of Rheumatic Fever
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2.4 million units IM single dose (Early Syphilis) OR 2.4 MU IM weekly x 3 doses (Late Latent); 1.2 MU q3-4w (Rheumatic)
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Single dose up to 3 weekly injections (or long-term prophylaxis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict deep IM injection in ventrogluteal site; monitor post-injection 30 min for vasovagal and anaphylactic collapse

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Moderate Streptococcal Pharyngitis, Diphtheria & Uncomplicated Pneumonia
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 600,000 to 1.2 million units IM daily in 1–2 divided doses
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Aspirate prior to injection to avoid accidental intravascular deposition; observe for Hoigne syndrome and local induration

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Streptococcal Pharyngitis / Tonsillitis & Rheumatic Fever Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg PO every 6 to 8 hours (or 250 mg PO q6h for mild infection; pediatric: 25–50 mg/kg/day divided)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Administer on empty stomach 1 hour before or 2 hours after food for optimal bioavailability; assess symptom improvement in 48h

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia, Acute Otitis Media & H. pylori Eradication
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg to 875 mg PO q12h OR 500 mg PO q8h (High-dose otitis media: 80–90 mg/kg/day; H. pylori: 1 g BID)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High clinical tolerability; monitor respiratory resolution; verify adherence with twice-daily dosing schedules

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Listeria monocytogenes Meningitis & Intrapartum Group B Strep (GBS) Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 2 g IV every 4 hours (Meningitis) / 2 g IV initial load then 1 g IV q4h until delivery (GBS)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Standard guideline partner with Gentamicin for synergy against Listeria; observe for hypersensitivity and rash

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) Skin & Soft Tissue Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg PO q6h (Mild/Moderate) OR 1 g to 2 g IV q4–6h (Severe bacteremia/osteomyelitis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO, IV or IM every 6 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Take oral doses on empty stomach (1h pre-meal); monitor IV access for thrombophlebitis; assess CBC and transaminases

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Localized MSSA Impetigo, Folliculitis, Mastitis & Post-Surgical Wound Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 250 mg to 500 mg PO every 6 hours (pediatric: 25–50 mg/kg/day divided q6h)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict instruction to ingest with full glass of water and remain upright for 30 minutes; take on empty stomach

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe MSSA Bacteremia, Acute Osteomyelitis, Septic Arthritis & Staphylococcal Cellulitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg PO q6h OR 1 g to 2 g IV every 6 hours (extended to 2 g q4h in endocarditis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High-affinity staphylococcal therapy; monitor LFTs for late-onset cholestatic hepatitis; ensure correct infusion dilutions

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Healthcare-Associated Gram-Negative Rod Infections & Severe Sepsis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 3 g to 4 g IV every 4 to 6 hours (infused over 30–60 minutes or continuous infusion)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Evaluate daily serum electrolytes (sodium loading, hypokalemia); monitor coagulation and bleeding parameters

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis, Animal Bites & Community-Acquired Pneumonia
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 625 mg PO TID OR 1 g PO BID OR 1.2 g IV q8h (High-dose respiratory: 2 g PO BID ER)
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO or IV every 8 to 12 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Administer at start of meals to minimize gastrointestinal distress and enhance clavulanate absorption; monitor diarrhea and LFTs

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Intra-Abdominal Infections, Pelvic Inflammatory Disease & A. baumannii Sepsis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1.5 g to 3 g IV/IM every 6 hours (1.5g = 1g ampicillin + 0.5g sulbactam; 3g = 2g + 1g)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High efficacy against sulbactam-susceptible Acinetobacter; monitor bowel habits for CDAD and renal indices

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP/VAP), Febrile Neutropenia & Severe Intra-Abdominal Sepsis
