indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 4.5 g IV every 6 hours (standard 30-min infusion) OR 3.375 g to 4.5 g IV q8h extended 4-hour infusion
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Extended 4-hour infusions optimize time above MIC; monitor daily CrCl and BUN; caution with concurrent vancomycin AKI risk

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Upper/Lower Respiratory Infections & Post-Operative Gynecologic Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1000 mg PO BID (750mg amox / 250mg sulb) OR 1.5 g to 3 g IV every 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO, IV or IM every 8 to 12 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Alternative in patients sensitive to clavulanate GI toxicity; monitor respiratory clinical response and local culture data

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Streptococcal Pharyngitis, Pertussis & Diphtheria (Carrier State)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 250 mg to 500 mg PO q6h (Adult) / 30–50 mg/kg/day PO divided q6h (Pediatric)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Alternative in severe beta-lactam allergy; monitor for motilin-mediated severe abdominal cramping and nausea; check ECG for QT interval

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP), Atypical Pathogens & Chlamydial Urethritis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg PO on Day 1, then 250 mg PO once daily on Days 2–5 OR 500 mg PO once daily for 3 days; Urethritis: 1 g PO single dose
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 500 mg / day (up to 1 g / day for specific indications)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Administer 500 mg IV over at least 60 min; long tissue elimination half-life (~68h); monitor baseline ECG in high-risk cardiac cohorts

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Helicobacter pylori Triple Therapy, Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis & MAC Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: H. pylori: 500 mg PO BID (with PPI + Amoxicillin) x 14 days; Respiratory: 250 mg to 500 mg PO q12h; IV: 500 mg q12h
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict review of co-medications for CYP3A4 substrate toxicity; reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <30 mL/min; monitor hepatic and renal indices

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Upper/Lower Respiratory Tract Infections, Acute Tonsillitis & Sinusitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 150 mg PO BID OR 300 mg PO once daily taken 15 minutes before meals; Pediatric: 5–8 mg/kg/day divided BID
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High tissue concentrations in lung parenchyma and tonsillar tissue; ingest on an empty stomach for maximum bioavailability; monitor LFTs in liver disease

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Maternal Toxoplasmosis (Acute Primary Infection During Pregnancy)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 3 g (9 million international units) PO daily administered as 1 g (3 MIU) PO TID
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Continuous throughout pregnancy until delivery (or amniocentesis confirmation)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Prevents vertical maternal-fetal transmission across the placenta; switch to Pyrimethamine-Sulfadiazine if fetal amniotic PCR is positive after 18 weeks

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (CABP - Macrolide-Resistant S. pneumoniae)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 800 mg PO once daily for 3 days (ultra-short 3-day oral course)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Novel Indian-developed lactolide targeting multidrug-resistant respiratory pathogens; excellent lung tissue-to-plasma ratio; evaluate clinical defervescence within 72h

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections (due to susceptible Gram-negative bacilli)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1 g (1000 mg) PO QID (every 6 hours) for 7–14 days; reduce to 500 mg QID if chronic or post-acute
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Historical urinary antiseptic; maintain high fluid intake; obtain baseline urine culture; discontinue immediately if severe headache, visual disturbance, or photophobia occurs

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Typhoid Fever (Enteric Fever), Bone/Joint Infections, Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections & Pyelonephritis
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Adolescent (≥18 years; Pediatric anthrax/complicated UTI only)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Typhoid: 500 mg PO BID x 7–14d; Bone/Joint: 500–750 mg PO BID or 400 mg IV q8–12h x 4–6 weeks; Pyelonephritis: 500 mg PO BID x 7d
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO / IV every 12 hours (q8h in severe)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Standard first-line agent for multi-susceptible enteric strains; monitor for tendinitis, Achilles pain, and peripheral neuropathy; separate oral doses from multivalent cations by 2–4 hours

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Lower RTI, Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID), Chronic Bacterial Prostatitis & Diarrheal Illness
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Respiratory: 400 mg PO/IV q12h x 7–10d; PID: 400 mg PO BID + Metronidazole x 14d; Prostatitis: 200–400 mg PO BID x 4–6 weeks; Diarrhea: 200–400 mg PO BID x 3–5d
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Broad-spectrum empiric mainstay across Indian inpatient and outpatient settings; monitor ECG for QT prolongation if co-prescribed with antiarrhythmics; caution in elderly patients

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Uncomplicated / Complicated Urinary Tract Infections (UTI) & Acute Bacterial Diarrhea (Gastroenteritis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Uncomplicated UTI: 400 mg PO BID x 3 days; Complicated UTI: 400 mg PO BID x 10–21 days; Bacterial Diarrhea: 400 mg PO BID x 3–5 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 3–5 days (up to 21 days for complicated UTI)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High urinary and lumen concentration with limited systemic soft-tissue penetration; administer with a full glass of water 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals; monitor for tendon discomfort

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Systemic Bacterial Infections, Hospital-Acquired Gram-Negative Sepsis, Bone/Joint Infections & Refractory Prostatitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 400 mg PO or 400 mg IV slow infusion BID (every 12 hours) with meals; severe sepsis: 800 mg/day IV
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Excellent tissue distribution into bone matrix, prostate, and CSF; high incidence of Achilles tendinopathy requires vigilance; protect patient from solar radiation and UV exposure

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Lower Respiratory Tract Infections, Acute Pyelonephritis & Superficial Ocular Surface Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Systemic: 400 mg PO once daily; Ophthalmic: 1–2 drops into conjunctival sac q2–4h for 2 days, then QID for 5 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Pronounced phototoxicity danger: advise patients to avoid direct natural sunlight and artificial UV rays during and for several days after therapy; maintain active renal hydration

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP), Acute Pyelonephritis, Complicated Skin/Soft Tissue Infections & Acute Sinusitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Geriatric (≥18 years; Inhalation anthrax/plague pediatric exceptions)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: CAP: 500 mg PO/IV once daily x 7–14d OR 750 mg once daily x 5d; Pyelonephritis: 750 mg PO/IV once daily x 5d; Sinusitis: 500 mg once daily x 10–14d
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 5–14 days (up to 28 days for chronic prostatitis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Premier respiratory fluoroquinolone in Indian clinical protocols; active against penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae; monitor blood glucose closely in diabetics; watch for QT prolongation

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis (AECB) & Non-Extensive Community Skin/Soft Tissue Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Initial loading dose: 400 mg PO on Day 1, followed by 200 mg PO once daily for the remaining 9 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Long half-life enables convenient single daily dosing; significant QTcF prolongation profile—contraindicated in congenital long QT or hypokalemia; strict solar avoidance required

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia, Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections & Post-Operative Ophthalmic Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult (≥18 years; Ophthalmic drops safe in neonates/pediatrics ≥1 year)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Systemic: 400 mg PO or 400 mg IV once daily; Ophthalmic (0.5% drops): 1 drop TID for 7 days post cataract/refractive surgery
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO / IV once daily (q24h) / Ophthalmic topical
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Fourth-generation fluoroquinolone with anaerobic activity; hepatic clearance eliminates need for renal dose adjustment; high ocular tissue penetration; baseline ECG if multiple QT risk factors present

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Acute Bacterial Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis (ABECB) & Mild-to-Moderate CAP
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 320 mg PO once daily for 5 days (ABECB) OR 320 mg PO once daily for 7 days (CAP)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Potent dual DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV inhibition; observe for maculopapular cutaneous rash (discontinue immediately if rash appears); ingest with plenty of fluids with or without food

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections (ABSSSI) & Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia (CABP)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: ABSSSI: 300 mg IV q12h OR 450 mg PO q12h x 5–14 days; CABP: 300 mg IV q12h OR 450 mg PO q12h x 5–10 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Anionic charge retains antibacterial potency in acidic abscess fluid and phagolysosomes; potent anti-MRSA and anti-pseudomonal dual coverage; clean cardiac and phototoxicity safety record

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Bacterial Skin and Skin Structure Infections (ABSSSI including MRSA), Diabetic Foot Infections & Sepsis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 800 mg IV infusion BID (every 12 hours) OR 1000 mg PO BID (as Alalevonadifloxacin mesylate oral prodrug) for 7–14 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: DCGI/CDSCO approved novel Indian fluoroquinolone class; superior bactericidal activity against multi-drug resistant Gram-positive pathogens; no QTcF prolongation; evaluate clinical defervescence within 72h

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acne Vulgaris (Inflammatory Papulopustular Lesions) & Superficial Bacterial Folliculitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Topical 1% Cream / Gel: Apply thinly to cleaned and dried affected dermatological areas twice daily (BID) morning and night
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 4–8 weeks (up to 12 weeks for refractory acne)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Bactericidal against Cutibacterium acnes; low cross-resistance to macrolides and clindamycin; do not apply to open cuts, abrasions, or mucous membranes; avoid ocular contact

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Mixed Bacterial-Protozoal Diarrhea, Amoebic Dysentery, Pelvic Inflammatory Disease & Dental Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ofloxacin 200 mg + Ornidazole 500 mg PO BID x 5 days; IV: Ofloxacin 200 mg + Ornidazole 500 mg IV infusion BID x 3–5 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 3–5 days (up to 10 days for complex PID)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Synergistic FDC widely utilized across Indian outpatient clinics for mixed gastrointestinal and pelvic infections; strict abstinence from alcohol required to prevent disulfiram-like reactions

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Infectious Diarrhea, Amoebic Colitis, Bacillary Dysentery & Mixed Enteric Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Norfloxacin 400 mg + Tinidazole 600 mg PO BID taken 1 hour before or 2 hours after food for 3–5 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Standard retail gastrointestinal FDC across India; tinidazole provides rapid luminal clearance of Entamoeba histolytica; monitor for bitter taste and metallic tongue coating; avoid alcohol

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Infectious Diarrhea, Amoebiasis with Secondary Bacterial Infection & Mixed Dental/Gingival Abscesses
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg + Tinidazole 600 mg PO BID taken after meals for 5–7 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Potent broad-spectrum enteric FDC; effective against invasive Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter, and anaerobic protozoa; strictly avoid alcohol; ensure robust oral rehydration protocol

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Moderate-to-Severe Acne Vulgaris, Cholera (Vibrio cholerae) & Rickettsial Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Acne: 250–500 mg PO BID to QID; Cholera: 500 mg PO QID x 3 days; Syphilis (penicillin-allergic): 500 mg QID x 14 days
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Administer on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals) with 250 mL water; strictly avoid dairy, antacids, or iron supplements within 2 hours; evaluate cutaneous response at 6–8 weeks

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Superficial Dermatological Pyoderma, Trachoma & Systemic Chlamydial / Mycoplasma Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Systemic: 250–500 mg PO q6h; Topical: Apply 3% skin ointment 2–3 times daily; IM (if oral unfeasible): 250 mg q24h or 300 mg/day divided
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: PO / Topical / Deep IM every 6 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Deep gluteal IM administration only; avoid intravascular injection; take oral doses 1h pre-prandial; monitor for thrombophlebitis, local tissue necrosis, and photosensitivity reactions

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Superficial Ocular Infections (Bacterial Conjunctivitis, Trachoma) & Localized Skin Pyodermas
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ophthalmic: Apply 1% eye ointment into inferior conjunctival sac q2–4h to TID; Dermatological: Apply 3% topical ointment BID to TID
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 7–14 days (up to 4–6 weeks for Trachoma mass prophylaxis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: Topical / Ophthalmic application only (TID to QID)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Ophthalmic administration may cause transient visual blurring; cleanse application site prior to dermal use; discontinue if marked erythema, local hypersensitivity, or contact dermatitis occurs

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Pneumonia, Scrub Typhus, Urogenital Chlamydia, Lyme Disease & Falciparum Malaria Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Pediatric (>8 years; any age for life-threatening Rickettsia)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Standard: 100 mg PO/IV q12h on day 1, then 100 mg daily or BID; Scrub Typhus: 100 mg BID x 7 days; Chlamydia: 100 mg BID x 7 days; Malaria prophylaxis: 100 mg daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 7–14 days (up to 28 days for Lyme borreliosis)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Ingest with 250 mL water while standing or sitting upright; do not recline for ≥30 min (pill-induced esophageal ulceration prevention); broad safety in renal failure; advise sunscreen for UV photosensitivity

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Moderate-to-Severe Inflammatory Acne Vulgaris, Hidradenitis Suppurativa & Methicillin-Resistant S. aureus (MRSA) Skin Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Acne: 50–100 mg PO BID or 100 mg modified-release daily; MRSA/Systemic: 200 mg loading dose, then 100 mg PO/IV q12h
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Screen for vestibular symptoms (ataxia, vertigo, lightheadedness) especially in young women; monitor for drug-induced lupus, antinuclear antibodies (ANA), hepatic transaminases, and hyperpigmentation

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections (cIAI), Complicated Skin & Soft Tissue Infections (cSSTI) & Multidrug-Resistant (MDR) Hospital Sepsis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 100 mg IV initial loading dose, followed by 50 mg IV every 12 hours (infusion over 30–60 minutes); severe hepatic (Child-Pugh C): 25 mg IV q12h maintenance
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Reserved strictly for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE), ESBL, and MRSA; NOT indicated for bloodstream infections or HAP due to low serum levels and mortality signal; premedicate with antiemetic

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Respiratory Tract Infections, Urogenital Infections, Acne Vulgaris & Mixed Bacterial Infections with High Dysbiosis Risk
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1 Capsule (Doxycycline 100 mg + Lactic Acid Bacillus 5 Billion Spores) PO BID on day 1, then 1 Capsule PO once or twice daily after meals
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Probiotic component prevents antibiotic-associated diarrhea (AAD) and intestinal dysbiosis; take with liberal water in upright posture; separate from divalent multivalent cations by 2 hours

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Gram-Negative Sepsis, Hospital-Acquired / Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia (HAP/VAP) & Complicated UTIs
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 15–20 mg/kg IV once daily (extended-interval) or 7.5 mg/kg IV/IM q12h; neonates: 15–18 mg/kg q24–36h
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion (over 30–60 min) or IM every 24 hours (or q12h)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM) mandatory: measure trough (<5 mcg/mL) prior to 2nd or 3rd dose, peak (20–30 mcg/mL) 30 min post-infusion; baseline/serial serum creatinine and audiometry; adjust interval for CrCl <50 mL/min

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Enterococcal / Streptococcal Endocarditis Synergy, Intra-Abdominal Sepsis & Pyelonephritis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Synergy: 1 mg/kg IV/IM q8h or 3 mg/kg once daily; Sepsis/cUTI: 5–7 mg/kg IV once daily or 1.5–2 mg/kg q8h
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion (over 30–60 min) or IM every 8 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict TDM: target synergy trough <1 mcg/mL, once-daily trough <0.5–1 mcg/mL; monitor serum creatinine every 48–72h; discontinue immediately if acute kidney injury or vestibular ataxia/tinnitus develops

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Pseudomonas aeruginosa Sepsis / Severe Nosocomial Infections & Cystic Fibrosis Pulmonary Exacerbations
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Systemic: 5–7 mg/kg IV once daily or 1.5–2 mg/kg q8h; Inhalation (CF): 300 mg nebulized BID (alternating 28 days on / 28 days off)
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion / Inhalation (PARI-LC) every 8 to 24 hours (or BID inhaled)
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 7 mg/kg / day IV; 600 mg / day inhaled
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Systemic TDM: peak 20–30 mcg/mL (once-daily), trough <1 mcg/mL; for inhalation, administer post-bronchodilator; monitor FEV1, audiometry, and baseline/trough serum creatinine

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Urinary Tract, Intra-Abdominal, Biliary & Skin/Soft Tissue Infections Resistant to Gentamicin
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 4–6 mg/kg IV/IM once daily or 1.3–2.2 mg/kg q8h; UTIs (uncomplicated): 3 mg/kg once daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion (over 30–60 min) or IM every 8 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor serum creatinine twice weekly; measure trough (<2 mcg/mL) and peak (6–10 mcg/mL for divided doses); assess for early vestibular signs; dose reduction required in renal impairment

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB / Second-Line NTEP), Tularemia, Plague & Brucellosis Synergy
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Adolescent (≥15 years; NTEP pediatric protocols)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: TB: 15 mg/kg (typically 0.75–1.0 g) deep IM once daily (5–6 days/week); Plague/Tularemia: 1 g IM q12h; Brucellosis: 1 g IM daily with Doxycycline
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Deep IM Injection every 12 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 1000 mg / day (reduce to 500–750 mg in elderly >60 years)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: High-risk vestibular neurotoxicity: perform baseline and monthly audiometry/caloric tests; monitor BUN, serum creatinine, and complete blood counts; reduce dose/frequency if CrCl <50 mL/min

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Second-Line Therapeutic Regimens for Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis (MDR-TB) & Severe Hospital Sepsis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: MDR-TB: 15 mg/kg (usually 0.75–1.0 g) IM/IV once daily, 5–6 days per week; Sepsis: 15 mg/kg/day divided q8–12h
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Deep IM or IV Infusion (over 30–60 min) every 12 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Strict monthly audiometric screening for irreversible high-frequency sensorineural deafness; monitor serum creatinine twice monthly; discontinue immediately at earliest signs of ototoxicity or oliguria

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Urinary Tract Infections (cUTI) Including Pyelonephritis Caused by Carbapenem-Resistant / MDR Enterobacterales
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 15 mg/kg IV once daily (infused over 30 minutes); CrCl 30 to <60: 10 mg/kg q24h; CrCl 15 to <30: 10 mg/kg q48h
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion (over 30 minutes) every 24 to 48 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 7–10 days (up to 14 days for concurrent bacteremia)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Reserve strictly for MDR Enterobacterales cUTIs when alternative options are limited; monitor daily renal function; measure trough concentration prior to day 2 or 3 dose (target <3 mcg/mL)

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Visceral Leishmaniasis (Kala-Azar, NVBDCP Guidelines) & Intestinal Amoebiasis / Cryptosporidiosis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Kala-Azar: 11 mg base/kg (15 mg sulfate/kg) IM daily x 21 days (or 10 days with Liposomal Amphotericin B); Amoebiasis: 25–35 mg/kg/day PO divided in 3 doses with meals
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Deep IM (Kala-azar) or Oral (Amoebiasis) every 8 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: Oral: 2000 mg / day; IM: 11 mg/kg base/day
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Kala-azar protocol: monitor for local injection site pain, baseline liver/renal markers, and audiometric changes; oral protocol: monitor GI symptoms (nausea, abdominal cramps, diarrhea); take oral dose with meals

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Hepatic Encephalopathy (Hyperammonemia Reduction) & Preoperative Elective Bowel Cleansing / Sterilization
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Hepatic Encephalopathy: 4–12 g/day PO divided q4–6h (acute) or 1–2 g/day (maintenance); Bowel Prep: 1 g PO at 19h, 18h, and 9h prior to surgery alongside erythromycin base
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Oral every 4 to 8 hours (or scheduled preoperative protocol)
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Bowel prep: <24 hours; Hepatic coma: 5–6 days (acute episode)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Short-term use only (<14 days); monitor for mucosal absorption and systemic ototoxicity/nephrotoxicity especially in patients with co-existing hepatorenal syndrome; assess serum ammonia and hearing acuity

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Superficial Pyoderma, Impetigo, Infected Minor Abrasions, Wounds & Burns (often combined with Bacitracin/Polymyxin B)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Apply thin layer of 0.5% (5 mg/g) ointment/cream to cleansed affected area 1 to 3 times daily; cover with sterile dressing if appropriate
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: Apply thin film 1–3 times daily (limit treated area to <20% BSA)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Do not exceed 7 days continuous application to prevent contact sensitization and superinfection; discontinue if contact dermatitis, burning, or worsening erythema occurs; do not apply to extensive weeping burns

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: External Ocular Bacterial Infections (Bacterial Conjunctivitis, Blepharitis, Keratitis) & Post-Operative Ophthalmic Prophylaxis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Drops (0.3%): Instill 1–2 drops into affected eye(s) q4h (mild-to-moderate) or q1–2h (severe); Ointment (0.3%): Apply 1 cm ribbon into conjunctival sac BID–TID or at bedtime
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Ophthalmic Instillation every 2 to 4 hours (initially) then taper
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: Ophthalmic topical application up to q2h waking hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor for corneal re-epithelialization, conjunctival erythema, and eyelid edema; remove contact lenses during infection and wait 15 min after instillation before reinserting; taper frequency as infection clears

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Superficial Bacterial Eye Infections (Conjunctivitis, Blepharitis), Infected Skin Ulcers, Folliculitis & Eczematoid Dermatitis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ophthalmic: Instill 1–2 drops 0.3% solution q4h or apply 0.3% ointment BID–TID; Topical: Apply 0.1% cream/ointment to cleansed skin lesion 3–4 times daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Ophthalmic / Topical Dermal every 4 to 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Evaluate for localized hypersensitivity, ocular burning, and epithelial toxicity; avoid large body surface area application in open ulcerations to prevent systemic absorption; sterile application technique

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Superficial Cuts, Minor Thermal Burns, Traumatic Wounds, Paronychia, Ulcers & Post-Surgical Skin Graft Dressing
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Pediatric (all ages for localized minor wounds)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Cream/Ointment (1% w/w): Apply thin layer evenly over lesion 1 to 3 times daily; Gauze Tulle Dressing: Apply single sterile impregnated layer directly over wound under sterile bandage
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 1–3 applications per day (avoid extensive surface dressing >10% BSA)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Cleanse wound debris prior to application; monitor for localized hypersensitivity and contact dermatitis; do not apply to extensive second/third-degree burns or open tympanic membranes; replace dressing daily or per surgical protocol

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Primary and Secondary Bacterial Cutaneous Infections (Pyoderma, Impetigo Contagiosa, Ecthyma, Furunculosis & Infected Wounds)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Cream/Ointment (0.1% w/w): Apply thin film gently to affected skin lesions 2 to 3 times daily; may cover with sterile gauze
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor for skin irritation, itching, or contact hypersensitivity; discontinue if rash or stinging develops; inspect for bacterial clearance at day 7; avoid application near eyes or mucous membranes

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Pneumocystis jirovecii Pneumonia (Treatment/Prophylaxis) & Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: PJP Treatment: 15–20 mg/kg/day TMP (75–100 mg/kg/day SMX) IV/Oral divided q6–8h; UTI: 1 DS tablet (800/160 mg) PO q12h
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Oral / IV Infusion every 6 to 12 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: UTI: 3–7 days; PJP Treatment: 21 days; PJP Prophylaxis: indefinite/continuous
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor serum potassium (risk of hyperkalemia), CBC with differential (bone marrow suppression), and renal function; ensure adequate oral fluid intake to prevent crystalluria; adjunctive corticosteroids indicated for severe PJP if PaO2 <70 mmHg.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria (in Combination with Artesunate - ACT) & IPTp
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Single dose: Sulfadoxine 25 mg/kg + Pyrimethamine 1.25 mg/kg (Adult: 3 tablets containing 1500 mg Sulfadoxine / 75 mg Pyrimethamine stat) combined with Artesunate (3 days)
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: 1 day (Single Stat Dose in combination regimen)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Ensure co-administration with oral artesunate for 3 days per national vector-borne disease control program; administer with water after food; report any rash or mucosal lesions immediately; do not use for malaria prophylaxis in non-immune travelers due to SJS risk.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Ulcerative Colitis (Mild-to-Moderate Active Flare / Maintenance) & Rheumatoid Arthritis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ulcerative Colitis: 3–4 g/day orally in divided doses (initial 500 mg–1 g q6–8h titrated up); Maintenance: 2 g/day; Rheumatoid Arthritis: 2 g/day divided BID
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Swallow tablets whole after meals with full glass of water; co-prescribe folic acid 1 mg/day; monitor CBC and liver function biweekly for first 3 months, then monthly for 3 months, then every 3 months; monitor urinalysis for crystalluria and renal cast formation.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Prevention and Treatment of Wound Sepsis in Second- and Third-Degree Thermal Burns
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Apply sterile 1% cream approximately 1/16th inch (1–2 mm) thickness directly to debrided, cleansed burn area 1 to 2 times daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Topical Dermal Application every 12 to 24 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Until satisfactory healing occurs or site is ready for skin grafting
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: Reapply as needed to keep burn wound covered (avoid >20% BSA in renal failure)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Maintain burn wound continuously covered with cream; reapply immediately if rubbed off; monitor CBC for transient silver-induced leukopenia (typically resolves without discontinuation); inspect for localized fungal superinfection.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Acute Bacterial Conjunctivitis, Blepharitis, Trachoma & Superficial Ocular Surface Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Ophthalmic Solution (10%): Instill 1 to 2 drops into affected eye(s) every 2 to 3 hours initially, tapering frequency as infection improves
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Cleanse exudate from eyes prior to instillation; do not touch dropper tip to eyelid; discard solution if dark brown or precipitated; not effective against viral or fungal keratitis; remove contact lenses before instillation.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Adjunctive Topical Antimicrobial Therapy for Severe Full-Thickness Thermal Burn Wounds
indications_dosing_matrix.Patient Cohort: Adult & Pediatric (under burn critical care protocol)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Apply 8.5% cream (or 5% topical solution) 1/16th inch thick to burn wounds once or twice daily with sterile gloved hand
indications_dosing_matrix.Typical Duration: Until burn wound is re-epithelialized or grafted
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Monitor serum electrolytes and acid-base balance (arterial blood gases) regularly for metabolic acidosis and respiratory hyperventilation due to carbonic anhydrase inhibition; pre-medicate with analgesics for application burning; discontinue temporarily if severe acidosis develops.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Severe Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP/VAP), Septic Shock & Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1 g IV every 8 hours (standard); high-dose 2 g IV every 8 hours (extended 3-hour infusion) for bacterial meningitis or MDR Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion over 30 min (or extended over 3 hours) every 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 6 g per day (in meningitis or severe MDR infections)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Utilize extended 3-hour infusions to maximize time above MIC (T > MIC); adjust dosage strictly based on estimated CrCl; do not co-administer with valproic acid due to precipitous loss of seizure control; monitor renal panel and differential CBC.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Polymicrobial Severe Intra-Abdominal Sepsis, Gynecologic Infections & Complicated Bone/Joint Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg IV every 6 hours or 1 g IV every 8 hours; severe life-threatening: 1 g IV every 6 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion over 40 to 60 minutes every 6 to 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 4 g per day (or 50 mg/kg/day, whichever is less)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Infuse slowly over 40–60 minutes (rapid infusion induces nausea and vomiting); monitor neurological status closely for seizure activity (especially in elderly patients, stroke history, or renal impairment); check baseline and periodic renal/liver chemistry.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections, Acute Pelvic Infections & Diabetic Foot Soft Tissue Infections
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1 g IV/IM once daily (Adult); Pediatric (3 months to 12 years): 15 mg/kg IV/IM twice daily (max 1 g/day)
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion over 30 minutes or deep IM injection once daily
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Ideal once-daily outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) agent; not active against Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Enterococcus; reduce dose to 500 mg once daily if CrCl ≤50 mL/min; monitor for injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity, and diarrhea.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Intra-Abdominal Infections (cIAI) & Complicated Urinary Tract Infections / Pyelonephritis
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 500 mg IV every 8 hours as an infusion over 1 hour
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion over 60 minutes every 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Contraindicated in ventilator-associated pneumonia (higher mortality reported); adjust dose in renal impairment (250 mg q8h if CrCl 30–50; 250 mg q12h if CrCl 10–29); monitor renal markers, serum sodium, and valproate concentrations.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Community-Acquired Respiratory Tract Infections, Acute Bacterial Sinusitis & Uncomplicated UTI (Step-Down / Outpatient)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: Adult: 200 mg to 300 mg orally TID (every 8 hours); severe/refractory infection: 300 mg TID
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: Oral every 8 hours (with or without food)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Reserve for culture-proven multi-drug resistant pathogens or when standard oral beta-lactams have failed; monitor for gastrointestinal side effects (loose stools, nausea); avoid inappropriate over-the-counter dispensing to prevent community carbapenem resistance.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Complicated Urinary Tract Infections (cUTI / Pyelonephritis) & Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia Caused by CRE (KPC-Producers)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 4 g IV (Meropenem 2 g + Vaborbactam 2 g) every 8 hours administered as an extended 3-hour IV infusion
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Extended Infusion over 3 hours every 8 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 12 g per day (6 g Meropenem / 6 g Vaborbactam)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Perform antimicrobial susceptibility testing to verify serine carbapenemase (KPC) production; ineffective against metallo-beta-lactamases (NDM, VIM) or OXA-48; mandatory 3-hour infusion pump delivery; titrate rigorously based on serial renal function.

indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Indication: Hospital-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia / VAP & cUTI Caused by Multi-Drug Resistant Gram-Negative Bacilli (including Pseudomonas)
indications_dosing_matrix.Standard Regimen / Dose: 1.25 g IV (Imipenem 500 mg + Cilastatin 500 mg + Relebactam 250 mg) every 6 hours as a 30-minute IV infusion
indications_dosing_matrix.Route & Frequency: IV Infusion over 30 minutes every 6 hours
indications_dosing_matrix.Max Daily Ceiling: 5 g per day (2 g Imipenem / 2 g Cilastatin / 1 g Relebactam)
indications_dosing_matrix.Clinical Protocol & Monitoring: Evaluate renal clearance prior to initiation; relebactam restores imipenem susceptibility against KPC-producing Enterobacterales and AmpC/efflux-derepressed Pseudomonas aeruginosa; observe for CNS hyperexcitability and seizures; track liver function tests.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (1 g & 2 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: 1g with 9.6 mL Sterile Water/NS (100 mg/mL); dilute in 50–100 mL NS or D5W. IM: 1g with 2.1 mL 1% Lidocaine HCl (350 mg/mL).
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer over 30 min. IM Injection: Deep gluteal injection (never inject lidocaine diluent IV).
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store powder at 20–25°C protected from light. Reconstituted IV bag stable 24 hours at room temp, 3 days at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: ABSOLUTE INCOMPATIBILITY: Never mix, infuse, or flush with Ringer's Lactate, Hartmann's, or any calcium-containing fluid (fatal lung/kidney precipitate risk).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (1 g Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 1g with 2.5 mL SWFI; further dilute in 50–100 mL NS or D5W for infusion
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Over 30–60 min. Direct IV Push: Very slow over 3–5 min. IM: Deep into large muscle mass.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store vial at 20–25°C. Reconstituted solution stable 24h at room temp and 10 days refrigerated (2–8°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with aminoglycosides (physically separate line/timing); do not mix with ampicillin or bleomycin.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Powder for Injection (750 mg & 1.5 g Vials) & Film-Coated Tablet (500 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: 750mg with 8 mL / 1.5g with 16 mL SWFI; dilute in 50–100 mL NS/D5W. IM: 750mg with 3 mL SWFI. Oral: Take with food.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer over 30 min. IM: Deep gluteal injection. Oral: Swallow whole, do not crush.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Vials: Store <25°C. Reconstituted IV solution stable 24h at room temp, 48h at 2–8°C. Tablets: Room temp away from moisture.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with sodium bicarbonate (fluids with pH >8.0 can accelerate decomposition); separate from aminoglycosides.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (1 g & 2 g Vials with Carbon Dioxide release)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 1g with 10 mL / 2g with 10 mL SWFI (effervescence occurs; vent needle); dilute in 100 mL NS or D5W.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Over 30 min or continuous extended infusion over 3–4 hrs. IM: Deep intragluteal injection.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store powder below 25°C protected from light. Reconstituted solution stable 24h at room temp and 7 days at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Contains carbonate; releases CO2 upon dilution. Incompatible with vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and ranitidine in same line.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Powder for Injection (1 g & 2 g Vials with L-Arginine)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 1g with 10 mL / 2g with 10 mL SWFI, NS, or D5W; further dilute in 50–100 mL infusion bag (NS, D5W).
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Intermittent over 30 min (or extended over 3–4 hrs). IM: Deep IM (rarely used due to volume).
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Vials store at 2–25°C protected from light. Reconstituted IV solution stable 24h at room temp and 7 days at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with vancomycin (precipitate formation; must flush thoroughly between infusions), gentamicin, metronidazole.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (600 mg Single-Use Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 600mg vial with 20 mL SWFI or NS; gently swirl to dissolve; dilute total volume into 250 mL NS, D5W, or LR.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion only: Administer over 60 min. Do not give as rapid IV bolus or IM injection.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store dry vial at 25°C (excursions permitted to 15–30°C). Reconstituted infusion bag stable 6h at room temp, 24h refrigerated.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Compatibility not established with many IV additives; infuse through dedicated line or flush line prior to and post-infusion.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Powder for Injection (1 Million & 5 Million Unit Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 5 MU vial with 8.2 mL SWFI or NS (gives 500,000 U/mL); dilute further into 50–100 mL NS or D5W. IM: 1 MU in 1.6 mL SWFI.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer intermittent infusion over 30–60 min or continuous infusion. IM: Deep into large gluteal muscle.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Dry vials store below 25°C. Reconstituted aqueous solution stable 24h at room temp and up to 7 days refrigerated (2–8°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with aminoglycosides (inactivation via aminolysis); incompatible with amphotericin B and vancomycin in same line.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Injectable Repository Suspension (1.2 Million & 2.4 Million Unit Prefilled Syringe / Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Precipitated aqueous suspension; no diluent mixing required for prefilled syringes. Vials: Shake vigorously with provided SWFI.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IM Injection Only: Administer deep IM into the upper outer quadrant of the buttock or ventrogluteal site with 18–20 gauge needle.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store refrigerated at 2–8°C. Do not freeze. Protect from direct heat and light. Stable until package expiration date.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: FATAL IF GIVEN IV: Absolute contraindication to IV/intra-arterial administration (causes cardiac arrest, gangrene, and death).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Sterile Aqueous Suspension for IM Injection (600,000 & 1.2 Million Unit Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Shake vial vigorously prior to withdrawal. If provided as powder, reconstitute with SWFI per vial label instructions.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IM Injection Only: Deep intramuscular injection into upper outer quadrant of buttock; slow steady injection pressure.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store in refrigerator at 2–8°C. Do not freeze. Reconstituted suspension stable 24 hours at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: IM ONLY: Inadvertent IV injection produces immediate Hoigne syndrome (hallucinations, seizures, cyanosis) and embolism.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (250 mg & 500 mg) & Oral Solution (125 mg / 5 mL & 250 mg / 5 mL)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: No reconstitution for tablets. Oral Solution: Add specified volume of purified water in two portions; shake vigorously.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Administer on an empty stomach at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals with water.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Tablets: Store at 20–25°C in tight container. Reconstituted oral suspension stable 14 days under refrigeration (2–8°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Food significantly impairs absorption; do not administer concurrently with acidic fruit juices or carbonated beverages.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Capsules (250 mg, 500 mg), Chewable Tablets & Powder for Oral Suspension (125 mg/5 mL, 250 mg/5 mL)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Add measured sterile water to dry powder bottle in two aliquots, shaking thoroughly between additions to fill mark.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Take at evenly spaced intervals with or without food (absorption is unaffected by food intake).
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Capsules/Tablets: Store at room temp (<25°C). Reconstituted oral suspension stable 14 days refrigerated (preferred) or 7 days at room temp.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Stable in presence of gastric acid; incompatible if mixed into alkaline IV solutions (if injectable amoxicillin utilized).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Powder for Injection (500 mg & 1 g Vials) & Capsules (250 mg, 500 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 1g vial with 10 mL SWFI (100 mg/mL); dilute immediately in 50–100 mL NS (use within 1 hour). IM: 1g with 3.5 mL SWFI.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Push: Slowly over 10–15 min. IV Infusion: Over 30–60 min. Oral: Take on empty stomach 1h pre-meal or 2h post-meal.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Unreconstituted vials store <25°C. Reconstituted IV solution in NS must be infused within 1 hour due to rapid beta-lactam hydrolysis.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Rapidly degrades in dextrose/glucose solutions (do NOT use D5W as diluent); physically incompatible with aminoglycosides.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Capsules (250 mg & 500 mg) & Lyophilized Powder for Injection (500 mg & 1 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 1g with 20 mL SWFI; dilute in 100 mL NS or D5W. IM: 500mg in 2 mL SWFI. Oral: Ingest whole with water.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer over 30–40 min. Direct IV: Slow over 3–5 min. IM: Deep into gluteal muscle. Oral: 1h before food.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Capsules store <25°C protected from moisture. Reconstituted IV infusion stable 24 hours at room temperature in NS.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Severe vein irritation; ensure complete dissolution and flush vein before and after infusion; incompatible with aminoglycosides.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Capsules (250 mg & 500 mg) & Powder for Oral Suspension (62.5 mg / 5 mL)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Reconstitute oral suspension with measured water; shake vigorously until homogeneous suspension forms.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Take with full glass (240 mL) of water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals; remain upright 30 min.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Capsules store at 20–25°C in tightly closed moisture-proof containers. Reconstituted oral liquid stable 14 days refrigerated (2–8°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Severe risk of pill-induced esophageal ulceration if taken dry or lying down; food decreases peak serum concentrations by ~50%.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Capsules (250 mg, 500 mg) & Powder for Injection (500 mg, 1 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 1g with 20 mL SWFI; further dilute in 100 mL NS or D5W. IM: 500mg in 1.5–2 mL SWFI. Oral: Ingest 30–60 min pre-meal.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Over 30–60 min. Slow IV Injection: Over 3–5 min. IM: Deep intramuscularly. Oral: On empty stomach.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store dry powder vials below 25°C. Reconstituted IV solution stable for 24 hours at room temperature.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: High risk of chemical phlebitis; inspect dilution clarity; incompatible with aminoglycosides, amiodarone, and blood products.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (2 g, 3 g & 4 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 4g vial with 20 mL SWFI, NS, or D5W; further dilute in 50–100 mL NS or D5W for intermittent infusion.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Infuse over 30 minutes (or continuous IV infusion). Direct IV Push: Slow injection over 3–5 minutes.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store intact vials at room temperature (20–25°C). Reconstituted solution stable 24h at room temp and 48h at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with aminoglycosides (mutually inactivate; do not co-infuse or mix); incompatible with potassium-sparing fluids.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (625 mg, 1 g), Powder for Oral Suspension & Powder for Injection (1.2 g Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 1.2g vial with 20 mL SWFI; dilute into 50–100 mL NS. Oral Liquid: Add sterile water to mark; shake well.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer over 30–40 min (complete within 3–4 hours of mixing). Oral: Take at start of a meal.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Dry tablets store below 25°C in moisture-barrier blister. Reconstituted IV in NS stable max 4h at 25°C; oral suspension 7 days at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Do not mix IV formulation with dextrose, sodium bicarbonate, or blood products; clavulanate unstable in carbohydrate solutions.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (1.5 g & 3 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 1.5g (1g ampicillin / 0.5g sulbactam) with 3.2 mL SWFI; 3g with 6.4 mL SWFI; dilute into 50–100 mL NS.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer over 15–30 min. Direct IV Push: Slow over 10–15 min. IM: Deep into large muscle mass.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Vials store <25°C. Reconstituted IV solution in NS is stable 8 hours at room temperature and 48 hours at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Do not mix with dextrose/glucose containing solutions (accelerates degradation); incompatible with aminoglycosides and ciprofloxacin.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Lyophilized Powder for Injection (2.25 g & 4.5 g Vials with EDTA)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Reconstitute 4.5g vial with 20 mL SWFI, NS, or D5W; gently shake until clear; dilute into 50–150 mL NS or D5W.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Standard infusion over 30 minutes OR extended infusion over 4 hours (preferred in sepsis/ICU protocols).
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store unreconstituted vials at 20–25°C. Reconstituted infusion bag stable 24 hours at room temp and 7 days at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Y-site incompatible with Amphotericin B, Acyclovir, and Vancomycin (in certain concentrations; flush catheter between drugs).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Powder for Injection (1.5 g & 3 g Vials) & Film-Coated Tablets (375 mg, 1000 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 1.5g with 10 mL SWFI; dilute in 100 mL NS. Oral: Swallow tablets whole with water at mealtime.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Over 30–60 min. IM: Deep gluteal injection with appropriate reconstitution. Oral: Ingest with meals.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Dry powder vials store below 25°C protected from light. Reconstituted IV solution stable 24h at room temp in NS.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with aminoglycosides (inactivated by beta-lactam); do not mix with sodium bicarbonate or multivitamin solutions.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (250 mg & 500 mg), Oral Suspension & Lyophilized Powder for Injection (500 mg, 1 g Vials)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 500mg vial with 10 mL SWFI without preservatives (50 mg/mL); dilute into 250–500 mL NS or Normosol. IM: Avoid (severe pain).
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Slow intermittent infusion over 60 min or continuous over 24h. Oral: Take on empty stomach with full glass of water.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Tablets/Capsules: Store below 25°C protected from moisture. Reconstituted IV solution in NS stable 8h at room temp and 24h at 2–8°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with beta-lactams (penicillins/cephalosporins), heparin, chloramphenicol, and aminophylline in same line; rapidly precipitates at pH <5.5.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (250 mg & 500 mg), Powder for Oral Suspension (100 mg/5 mL, 200 mg/5 mL) & Lyophilized Powder for Injection (500 mg Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 500mg vial with 4.8 mL SWFI (100 mg/mL); shake thoroughly; further dilute in 250 mL (2 mg/mL) or 500 mL (1 mg/mL) NS, D5W, or LR.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Infuse 500 mg over at least 60 minutes (1 mg/mL over 3h, 2 mg/mL over 1h). Do NOT give as IV bolus or IM. Oral: With/without food.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Dry vials store <30°C. Reconstituted IV solution in 250/500 mL bag stable 24h at room temp and 7 days at 2–8°C. Oral liquid stable 10 days at 25°C.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Do not infuse other IV medications or solutions through the same line concurrently; incompatible with high pH fluids or concentrated electrolytes.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (250 mg & 500 mg), Extended-Release Tablets (500 mg), Powder for Oral Suspension & Lyophilized Powder for Injection (500 mg Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IV: Reconstitute 500mg vial with 10 mL SWFI (50 mg/mL); dilute further into at least 250 mL NS, D5W, or LR (do not use solutions containing benzyl alcohol).
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: IV Infusion: Administer slowly into large vein over at least 60 minutes. Oral: Swallow whole with food (improves absorption and prevents nausea).
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Dry vials store at 20–25°C protected from light. Diluted IV infusion solution stable 6 hours at room temp and 48 hours at 2–8°C. Oral liquid: Do not refrigerate.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with aminophylline, ampicillin, and furosemide; severe local vein irritation/phlebitis risk if infused rapidly or concentrated (<250 mL diluent).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (150 mg & 300 mg), Dispersible Tablets (50 mg) & Oral Suspension (50 mg / 5 mL)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Disperse dispersible tablets in 5–10 mL drinking water before drinking; reconstitute dry powder suspension with boiled cooled water to mark.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Ingest on an empty stomach at least 15 minutes before meals or 2 hours after food for optimal gastrointestinal absorption.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Tablets store below 25°C in moisture-resistant strip packaging. Reconstituted pediatric oral suspension stable 10 days at room temperature (<25°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Food significantly decreases bioavailability and absorption; co-administration with ergot alkaloids is strictly contraindicated (ergotism danger).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (1.5 Million IU & 3 Million IU), Capsules & Lyophilized Powder for Injection (1.5 Million IU Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: No reconstitution needed for tablets. IV: Reconstitute 1.5 MIU with 4 mL SWFI; further dilute into 100–250 mL 5% Dextrose (D5W) or 0.9% NS.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Take with plenty of water. IV Infusion: Slow intermittent intravenous infusion over at least 60 minutes.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets and powder vials below 25°C in a dry environment. Reconstituted IV infusion bag stable 12 hours at room temperature in D5W or NS.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with alkaline intravenous infusions; physically separate infusion lines from other antibiotic or cardiovascular medications.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (800 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Standard manufactured oral solid dosage form; no reconstitution required. Ingest with an adequate glass of water.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Administer once daily with or without food as a single 800 mg dose for 3 consecutive days. Swallow tablet whole; do not crush or chew.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets in original blister packaging at room temperature (15–30°C) protected from excessive moisture and direct sunlight. Stable through labeled expiry.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Unlike first-generation ketolides (telithromycin), does not interact with nicotinic acetylcholine receptors; evaluate concomitant drugs for QT interval additive effects.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (500 mg) & Oral Suspension (300 mg / 5 mL)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Standard manufactured solid oral tablet or suspension; shake suspension well before administration. Ingest with water.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Administer on an empty stomach 1 hour before meals or 2 hours after meals with a full glass of water.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store in tight, light-resistant containers at controlled room temperature (15–30°C). Reconstituted suspension stable 14 days at room temp.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Chelates with antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, calcium, iron salts, and zinc; separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (250 mg, 500 mg, 750 mg), IV Infusion (200 mg / 100 mL & 400 mg / 200 mL), Eye/Ear Drops (0.3% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: No reconstitution needed. IV: Ready-to-use infusion bags in 5% Dextrose or 0.9% NaCl; or dilute 10 mg/mL concentrate into 0.9% NS or D5W.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Ingest with water. IV Infusion: Infuse slowly over 60 minutes (400 mg dose over 60 min) into a large vein to minimize venous irritation.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Tablets store below 25°C protected from moisture. IV premix store between 5–25°C; do not freeze; protect from direct light until use.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Precipitates with alkaline solutions (heparin, furosemide, aminophylline); multivalent cation binding severely diminishes oral bioavailability.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (200 mg & 400 mg), IV Infusion (200 mg / 100 mL in D5W/NS), Eye Drops (0.3% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow tablets whole with water. IV: Ready-to-use solution in 100 mL bottles/bags (2 mg/mL concentration); no dilution required.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Take with or without food. IV Infusion: Slow intravenous infusion over at least 30 to 60 minutes for each 200 mg dose; avoid rapid bolus.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets and IV solutions below 25°C in original cartons protected from light. Discard unused portion of IV infusion bottles.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Incompatible with strong alkaline solutions and calcium-containing parenteral fluids; multivalent cations reduce oral absorption by >80%.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (400 mg) & Ophthalmic Solution (0.3% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Manufactured oral solid dosage form; swallow whole with water. Do not crush or chew film-coated tablets.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Administer on an empty stomach with a full glass of water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals; maintain daily urine volume >1200 mL.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store below 25°C in tightly sealed moisture-proof blister packs. Protect eye drops from direct sunlight and heat; discard 28 days post opening.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Co-administration with dairy products, antacids, sucralfate, or multivitamin minerals sharply impairs absorption; avoid urinary alkalinizers (crystalluria).

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (400 mg) & Solution for IV Infusion (400 mg / 5 mL ampoule for dilution)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Take tablets with meals to prevent GI upset. IV: Dilute 400 mg ampoule in 250 mL of 5% Dextrose in water (D5W); DO NOT use 0.9% NaCl (precipitates).
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Administer twice daily with breakfast and dinner. IV Infusion: Administer as a slow IV drip over 60 minutes every 12 hours.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets and ampoules protected from light and heat (<25°C). Diluted D5W IV solution is stable for 24 hours at room temperature.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Strictly incompatible with 0.9% Normal Saline or chloride-containing solutions (causes pefloxacin precipitation); severe solar photosensitivity.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (400 mg) & Ophthalmic Drops (0.3% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Solid oral tablet formulation; swallow whole with ample water. Ophthalmic: Ready-to-use sterile eye drop bottle.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Administer once daily in the morning with or without food. Ophthalmic: Instill 1–2 drops into affected eye(s) as prescribed.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store at controlled room temperature (15–30°C) away from direct light and excessive humidity. Keep bottle tightly closed.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Binding with polyvalent cations (aluminum, magnesium, sucralfate); extreme phototoxicity—patients must avoid direct sun exposure during therapy.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (250 mg, 500 mg, 750 mg), IV Infusion (500 mg / 100 mL & 750 mg / 150 mL in D5W), Eye Drops (0.5% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow whole with fluid. IV: Ready-to-use single-dose flexible containers in 5% Dextrose (5 mg/mL concentration); no mixing needed.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Ingest without regard to meals. IV Infusion: Administer by slow intravenous infusion: 500 mg over at least 60 minutes; 750 mg over at least 90 minutes.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets and IV containers at 20–25°C; excursions permitted to 15–30°C. Protect IV containers from light; single-use only.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Rapid IV injection causes severe hypotension and collapse; do not infuse through common line with sodium bicarbonate or alkaline additives; cation chelation.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Oral Tablets (100 mg & 200 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Solid oral compressed tablet; swallow whole with water. May be taken with or without food.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Administer once daily. Loading dose 400 mg on day 1 (two 200 mg tablets), followed by 200 mg once daily.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store at controlled room temperature (20–25°C) in moisture-proof blister packaging protected from ambient light.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Concomitant intake of aluminum/magnesium antacids or iron supplements markedly inhibits sparfloxacin absorption; phototoxicity precaution.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (400 mg), IV Infusion (400 mg / 250 mL in 0.8% Saline), Ophthalmic Solution (0.5% w/v)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow whole. IV: Ready-to-use 250 mL flex bag or glass bottle (1.6 mg/mL in 0.8% NaCl); do not dilute further or add other additives.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Take with or without food. IV Infusion: Administer as a slow constant intravenous infusion over at least 60 minutes. Do not infuse via rapid bolus.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets at 15–30°C. Store IV solution at 15–30°C; DO NOT refrigerate or freeze (causes precipitation of crystals); protect from light.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Physically incompatible with alkaline IV solutions; severe bioavailability drop with aluminum, magnesium, iron, calcium, and multivitamin supplements.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (320 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Solid oral film-coated tablet; swallow whole with a full glass of water. May be taken with or without meals.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Administer 320 mg once daily for 5 or 7 days as clinically indicated; maintain abundant fluid hydration.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets at room temperature (20–25°C); excursions permitted between 15–30°C. Protect from moisture and direct sunlight.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Chelates with aluminum, magnesium antacids, ferrous sulfate, and zinc; separate oral doses by taking gemifloxacin at least 2h before or 3h after cations.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Tablets (450 mg) & Lyophilized Powder for IV Injection (300 mg Vial)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow whole. IV: Reconstitute 300 mg vial with 10.5 mL of 5% Dextrose (D5W) or 0.9% NS; further dilute to 250–500 mL in D5W or NS.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Ingest with or without food. IV Infusion: Infuse diluted intravenous solution over 60 minutes every 12 hours.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Vials store at 20–25°C. Reconstituted and diluted IV infusion solution is stable for 24 hours at room temperature or 7 days refrigerated (2–8°C).
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Oral delafloxacin binds polyvalent cations (aluminum, magnesium, iron); IV formulation contains cyclodextrin—monitor renal function closely.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: IV Solution / Powder for Infusion (800 mg Vial) & Oral Prodrug Tablets (1000 mg Alalevonadifloxacin)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow prodrug tablets whole. IV: Reconstitute/dilute 800 mg with 100 mL 0.9% Normal Saline or 5% Dextrose in water.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Take twice daily with or without food. IV Infusion: Infuse 800 mg as a slow intravenous infusion over 90 minutes twice daily.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store vials and tablets below 25°C in dry conditions protected from direct sunlight. Diluted IV solution stable for 24 hours at room temperature.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Compatible with 0.9% NS and D5W; do not co-infuse with blood products, lipid emulsions, or unverified injectable medications.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Topical Cream (1% w/w) & Topical Gel (1% w/w) in Aluminum / Plastic Tubes (10 g & 15 g)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Topical: Ready-to-use semi-solid dermatological formulation. Wash and thoroughly dry affected acne-prone skin before application.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Topical Application: Apply a thin layer over the affected skin lesions twice daily (morning and evening); gently massage until absorbed.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store below 25°C; do not freeze. Keep tube cap tightly closed after each use to prevent oxidation and drying of the cream/gel vehicle.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: For external dermatological use only; avoid contact with eyes, mucous membranes, eyelids, and open lacerated wounds; avoid concurrent harsh peeling agents.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (Ofloxacin 200 mg + Ornidazole 500 mg) & IV Infusion (100 mL Bottle)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow whole with water. IV: Ready-to-use dual infusion bottle containing Ofloxacin 200 mg + Ornidazole 500 mg in 100 mL sterile solution.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral: Take after meals to reduce gastric irritation. IV Infusion: Administer as a slow IV drip over 45 to 60 minutes twice daily.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store tablets and IV infusion bottles below 25°C protected from light and heat. Do not freeze IV bottles; single-patient use.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Strictly avoid ethanol/alcoholic beverages during therapy and for 48h after completion (disulfiram-like acetaldehyde accumulation); cation interaction.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (Norfloxacin 400 mg + Tinidazole 600 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Solid oral combination tablet; swallow whole with an ample glass of water. Do not crush or chew bitter core.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Take twice daily (BID) 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals with water; maintain excellent daily fluid hydration.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store below 25°C in sealed aluminum foil blister packaging protected from ambient humidity and direct sunlight.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Strictly avoid alcohol or alcohol-containing elixirs during and for 72 hours after therapy (disulfiram-like syndrome); polyvalent cation chelation.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Film-Coated Tablets (Ciprofloxacin 500 mg + Tinidazole 600 mg)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Solid oral combination tablet; swallow whole with water. Take after food to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Ingest 1 tablet twice daily (BID) every 12 hours after meals; ensure hydration of 1.5–2 liters fluid per day.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store in dry, cool conditions below 25°C protected from light. Keep in original foil packaging until time of dose administration.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Avoid all alcoholic drinks during and for 72h post-treatment (severe disulfiram effect); oral bioavailability drastically inhibited by multivalent mineral cations.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Oral Capsules / Tablets (250 mg & 500 mg Tetracycline HCl) & Topical Skin Ointment (3% w/w)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Oral: Swallow whole with 250 mL plain water. Topical: Ready-to-use ointment; clean and dry area before applying.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Oral Administration: Ingest on an empty stomach (1h before or 2h after meals) in an upright sitting or standing position. Topical: Apply thin layer to affected skin 2–3 times daily.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store capsules and ointment below 25°C in airtight containers protected from moisture and light. Expired tetracycline degrades into epitetracycline/anhydrotetracycline causing Fanconi-like nephrotoxicity.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Severe chelation interaction: completely incompatible with divalent/trivalent cations (aluminum, calcium, magnesium antacids, oral iron, zinc, milk/dairy); avoid co-administration within 2–3 hours.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: IM Injection Solution (50 mg/mL & 125 mg/mL with 2% Lidocaine), Capsules (250 mg), Topical / Ophthalmic Ointment (3% & 1%)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: IM: Ready-to-use solution containing local anesthetic (lidocaine HCl) to diminish injection pain. Do not dilute with calcium-containing intravenous fluids.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Deep IM Injection only: Administer slowly into large muscle mass (gluteal region); strictly avoid IV/SC injection. Oral: Ingest 1h before food. Topical: Apply thin film BID–TID.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store ampoules/vials between 15–25°C protected from light. Discard discolored solutions. Store topical and ophthalmic tubes below 25°C; do not freeze.
formulations_administration.Critical Compatibility Alerts: Contraindicated for IV administration (causes severe local thrombophlebitis). Chelation with metal ions, calcium gluconate, and dairy. Severe injection site pain and sterile abscess risk.

formulations_administration.Dosage Form & Strength: Topical Skin Ointment (3% w/w) & Sterile Ophthalmic Eye Ointment (1% w/w in 3.5 g / 5 g Tubes)
formulations_administration.Reconstitution Diluent & Volume: Ready-to-use semi-solid topical/ophthalmic preparation. No reconstitution or diluent required. Ensure tip of tube does not contact skin or ocular surface.
formulations_administration.Administration Route & Infusion Rate: Ophthalmic: Instill ribbon (approx. 1 cm) into inferior conjunctival fornix 2–4 times daily. Dermatological: Cleanse target lesion and apply thin film 2–3 times daily.
formulations_administration.Storage & Reconstituted Stability: Store below 25°C in original crimped aluminum tube; do not freeze. Discard eye ointment 30 days after opening to prevent microbial contamination.
